set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Many chemical processes involve substances in either the liquid or the gaseous state.
 Which of the following statements is correct?
options: A specific mass of a gas has a fixed volume at room temperature
B. A specific mass of a liquid has a fixed volume at room temperature
C. 25 cm 3  of gas contains more particles than 25 cm 3  of liquid
D. Liquid particles placed inside a sealed container have fixed positions
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  
 • A fixed mass of liquid at room temperature has a  definite volume .
 A  is incorrect as gases diffuse and occupy different  volumes  depending on the  temperature  and  pressure .
 C  is incorrect as  concentrations  of either the liquid or gas can change this relationship.
 D  is incorrect as liquid particles have the ability to  move  and  slide  around each other which gives them the ability to  flow .

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The following four statements describe the arrangement of particles in a substance.
 | 1
 | Particles are moving in all directions
 |
 | 2
 | Particles are arranged in neat rows
 |
 | 3
 | Particles can move past each other
 |
 | 4
 | Particles vibrate about their positions
 |
 Which of the four statements describe the arrangement of particles in a solid?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Particle theory shows that particles in a solid are arranged in  rows  forming a  regular pattern.
 • The particles cannot move in a solid but they do  vibrate.
 A  is incorrect as particles in a solid cannot move as described in statement 1.
 C  is incorrect as particles in a solid cannot move as described in statements 1 and 3
 D  is incorrect as statement 4 also applies to particles in a solid.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Ionic compounds are formed when a metal reacts with a nonmetal.
 Which two elements combine to form this kind of compound?
 | Element
 | Electronic structure
 |
 | Q
 | 2.4
 |
 | R
 | 2.8
 |
 | S
 | 2.8.1
 |
 | T
 | 2.8.7
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • Q  is carbon;  R  is neon;  S  is sodium and  T  is chlorine.
 • Each atom of sodium has  1  outer shell electron and each atom of chlorine has  7  outer electrons.
 • A sodium atom donates  one  electron to a chlorine atom and they form the ionic compound  sodium chloride  (NaCl) where each obtains a full outer shell.
 B  and  C  are   incorrect as these options contain R which is neon, a  noble gas  that does not combine with other elements.
 D  is incorrect as carbon and chlorine are both nonmetals and combine via  covalent  bonds, not ionic.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Atoms P and Q have electronic structures as shown in the diagram. They react together to form a covalent compound.
  What is the formula of the compound?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Element  P  is hydrogen and  Q  is nitrogen, both are non-metals.
 • Nitrogen has  5  outer electrons and requires  3  more to have an  octet .
 • Hydrogen has 1 electron in its outer shell, but since it's the first shell it requires only 2 electrons to be full, therefore each hydrogen atom requires just  1 more  electron to achieve a full outer shell.
 • 3 atoms of H combine with 1 N and both atoms achieve full outer shells as shown.
  A ,  C  and  D  are incorrect as the combinations in these formulae do not provide a full outer shell for each atom.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which of the following statements about graphite and diamond are incorrect?
 | 1
 | They are allotropes of carbon.
 |
 | 2
 | They both conduct electricity.
 |
 | 3
 | They form different numbers of bonds within their structures.
 |
 | 4
 | They have different uses.
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Graphite can conduct electricity as it has  delocalised electrons  that can move and carry charge.
 • In diamond all of the outer shell electrons in the carbon atoms are used in bonding so it does not conduct electricity as there are no free electrons.
 A, C  and  D  are incorrect as these properties are true for both graphite and diamond.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Ammonia is manufactured by the reaction of hydrogen and nitrogen in the Haber process, as shown in the equation below:
 N 2  + 3 H 2  → 2 NH 3
 16.8 tonnes of ammonia can be produced from 14 tonnes of nitrogen.
 How much nitrogen is needed to produce 51 tonnes of ammonia?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because
 | Step
 | Working out
 |
 | 1
 | The ratio of N 2  : NH 3  is  14 : 16.8. Divide across by the smallest number (14) to find the simplest  ratio .
 | The ratio of N 2  : NH 3  is   1 : 1.2.
 So for every 1 tonne of nitrogen,  1.2  tonnes of ammonia are produced.
 |
 | 2
 | Divide the amount of NH 3  desired (51 tonnes) by 1.2 to calculate the amount of nitrogen required.
 | 
 |
 B ,  C  and  D  are incorrect as these options do not give the correct amount.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Dilute sulfuric acid is electrolysed using inert electrodes. 
 What are the products of this electrolysis?
 |  
 | cathode
 | anode
 |
 | A
 | oxygen
 | sulfur 
 |
 | B
 | hydrogen
 | sulfur dioxide
 |
 | C
 | oxygen
 | hydrogen
 |
 | D
 | hydrogen
 | oxygen
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • The ions present in sulfuric acid are H +  and SO 4 2-
 • The ions present in water are H +  and OH - 
 • The positive hydrogen ions are attracted to the cathode (negative electrode) where they gain electrons to form hydrogen gas 
 2H +   +   2e -     ⟶   H 2
 • At the anode, oxygen is produced unless a halide ion is present in which case a halogen is produced 
 4OH –     ⟶    O 2    +   2H 2 O   +   4e –
 A  is incorrect as the oxygen is made at the anode, not the cathode and sulfur is not made at the anode
 B  is incorrect as sulfur is not produced at the anode
 C  is incorrect as the products are correct but they have been formed at the incorrect electrode

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which metal could  not  be used for electroplating by using an aqueous solution?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
  •  In electrolysis of aqueous solutions only one type of ion can be discharged at each electrode.
 • The H +  and OH -  ions produced by the dissociation of water in aqueous solutions compete with the other ions in solution.
 • At the cathode , the  more reactive  a metal is the  more it tends to remain as ions  in solution.
 • For electroplating to take place, the metal which is being used as the  coating  must be  unreactive.
 • Sodium could not be used for this purpose as it is too reactive.
 A, B  and  C  are incorrect as they could all be used as these metals are unreactive and are commonly used for electroplating.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Winston Churchill, a British Prime Minister, had his false teeth electroplated with gold.
 The teeth were coated with a thin layer of carbon and were then placed in the apparatus shown.
  |

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • In electroplating, the  anode  is always the metal that is being used to coat the other metal.
 • Coating occurs as the  positive   metal   ions  are attracted to the object to be coated which is the  negatively   charged   cathode .
 • The object to be coated is thus the cathode which attracts the positive metal ions.
 • In the diagram terminal X is therefore negative.
 • The carbon powder must be graphite as it conducts electricity due to the free  electrons in between the layers of carbon atoms.
 A  is incorrect as diamond is a hard substance which does not conduct electricity.
 C  and  D  are incorrect as terminal X is negative, not positive.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following processes is endothermic?
options: B. The use of petrol in an engine.
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • The distillation of crude oil  requires energy  as the oil must first be heated up to vaporise the molecules.
 • Energy is taken into the system from the surroundings so the process is  endothermic .
 A, B  and  D  are incorrect as these processes all give out energy hence they are exothermic.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which graph correctly shows the effect of increasing the temperature on the rate of reaction between magnesium and sulfuric acid in which neither reactant runs out?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  
 • Increasing the reaction temperature increases the rate of reaction so the correct graph should show a  continuous   increase  in rate which is directly related to an increasing temperature.
 B  is incorrect as it shows a levelling off of the rate even though the temperature continues to increase.
 C  is incorrect as the shape of the graph indicates that the rate has decreased dramatically with an increasing temperature.
 D  is incorrect as it shows a decrease in rate as the temperature increases.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A student was investigating the rate of reaction between acid and metals. The experimental set-up is shown below.
  Which test tube would give the quickest reaction?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  
 • Test tubes  A  and  B  contain  concentrated  acid.
 • Iron in test tube  A  is  more   reactive  than copper in  B , so  A  is the test tube which will react the fastest.
 B  is incorrect as the relative reactivity of the metals outweighs the greater surface area of the metal in B, compared to A.
 C  and  D  are incorrect as the acid used in these test tubes is dilute hence the rate of reaction will be slower.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Three reactions are shown below.
 • NO + O 3  → NO 2  + O 2
 • 2C + O 2  → 2CO
 • 2MgO + O 2  → 2MgO 2
 Which row correctly describes the process each reactant molecule undergoes?

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  
 • For NO and MgO, oxygen has been added so they are  oxidised :
 NO → NO 2             MgO → MgO 2
 • For O 3 , oxygen has been removed so it has been  reduced :
 O 3  → O 2
 B ,  C  and  D  are incorrect as these options do not correctly describe what happens to each reactant molecule.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A student is provided with an unmarked beaker containing a colourless solution and asked to identify it. The student decides to perform a series of reactions with the solution and record the observations.
 Which of these observations is not indicative of an acid?
options: A. The solution causes blue litmus to turn red.
B. On heating and the addition of copper oxide, the solution turns blue.
C. On the addition of ammonium carbonate, a colourless, pungent gas is released.
D. On the addition of a piece of magnesium, effervescence was produced and the magnesium piece ‘disappeared’ after a few minutes.
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  
 • Ammonium carbonate reacts with  alkalis  to produce the metal carbonate, ammonia gas and water. Ammonia gas is  colourless  and  pungent
 • An example is the reaction with sodium hydroxide:
 • (NH 4 ) 2 CO 3  + 2NaOH → Na 2 CO 3  + 2H 2 O + 2NH 3
 • The reaction is  not characteristic  of an acid as an acid-base neutralisation reaction produces a salt and water only.
 A  is incorrect as acids have pH values of  below 7  and will turn blue litmus paper  red .
 B  is incorrect as copper oxide is a weak base and will react with an acid forming  blue  hydrated copper salt. For example with sulfuric acid: 
 CuO +H 2 SO 4  → CuSO 4  + H 2 O
 D  is incorrect as magnesium reacts with acids producing the metal salt and  bubbles  of hydrogen gas. For example with hydrochloric acid:  
 Mg + 2HCl → MgCl 2  + H 2

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:

The correct answer is  A  
 • Methyl orange is red in acids and yellow in alkalis 
 • Sulfuric acid is an acid
 • Potassium hydroxide is an alkali
 B  is incorrect as universal indicator can turn a variety of colours, and is usually blue or purple in alkalis depending on alkali strength
 C  is incorrect as litmus is red in acids and blue in alkalis
 D  is incorrect as thymolphthalein is colourless in acids and blue in alkalis

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The early Periodic table was used to classify the known elements and was used to predict the properties of the elements that had not yet been discovered.
 Which row correctly describes how this was possible?
options: A. Elements in the same Period displayed similar properties.
B. The arrangement of the known elements provided trends in behaviour which was used to make predictions about the unknown elements.
C. Elements in different Groups displayed similar properties.
D. The unknown elements were used to fill the gaps in the original Periodic table and were placed according to their physical properties.
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  
 • There are  patterns  in the way the elements are arranged on the Periodic table, there are also patterns and trends in the  chemical   behaviour  of the elements.
 • In this way the Periodic table can be used to predict how an unknown element will behave and was used to  identify  them.
 A  is incorrect as elements in the same Period tend to behave  differently .
 C  is incorrect as elements in different Groups have  different   properties  as they have different outer shell  electron   configurations . Elements in the same group have the same number of electrons in their outer shell and share similar properties.
 D  is incorrect as the elements were positioned according to their  atomic   number  and  chemical  properties.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which statement about the Alkali metals is correct?
options: A. Potassium is more dense than lithium.
B. Lithium has a higher density than sodium.
C. Potassium is less reactive than sodium.
D. The melting point of sodium is higher than lithium.
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  
 • The atomic number of the elements increases and their properties change as you move down Group I.
 • Melting and boiling points and hardness  decrease  while their density  increases .
 • They become  more   reactive  due to increasing distance between the outermost  electrons and the nucleus, making it easier for the metals to lose their outer shell electron.
 • Potassium is below lithium in Group I so its density is  higher  than that of lithium.
 B  is incorrect as lithium is  less dense  than sodium as it is higher up in the group.
 C  is incorrect as potassium is below sodium in Group I and is thus  more   reactive .
 D  is incorrect as sodium has a  lower  melting point than lithium since it is lower down the group.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:

 |
 | D

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  
 • All the noble gases have  full outer shells . Helium, the first noble gas has only one shell which holds a maximum of 2 electrons.
 • The noble gases exist as  monatomic gases  as they do not combine with other elements due to their extremely  stable electronic configuration .
 • Their melting point and boiling points are  extremely low .
 B  and  D  are incorrect as the noble gases have full outer shells.
 C  is incorrect as the noble gases have extremely low boiling points. Helium for example boils at -269  o C which is the lowest of all the elements.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: The reactivity of the alkali metals increases moving down the group. Which statement explains this observation?
options: A. Decreasing distance between the nucleus and outer shell makes it easier for the metals to lose their valence electrons.
B. Increasing distance between the nucleus and outer shell makes it harder for the metals to lose their valence electrons.
C. Increasing distance between the nucleus and outer shell makes it easier for the metals to lose their valence electrons.
Decreasing distance between the nucleus and outer shell makes it easier for the metals to gain their valence electrons.
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  
 • There is an  extra shell  added for every period that you move down on the table which increases the distance from the  nucleus  to the  outermost   electrons .
 • The increasing distance makes it easier for the metals to lose their outer (valence) electrons as the  electrostatic forces of attraction  are  weakened  by the longer distance.
 A  is incorrect  as the distance  increases  moving down the group.
 B  is incorrect as the greater distance makes it  easier  to remove the valence electrons, not harder.
 D  is incorrect as Group 1 metals do not gain electrons, they lose them.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Element Q is a halogen which reacts with aqueous potassium bromide, as shown in the reaction below:
 Q 2  + 2 KBr → 2 KQ + Br 2
 Which row describes element Q?
 |  
 | More reactive than bromine

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  
 • Element Q has displaced bromine from the compound KBr, so it must therefore be more reactive than bromine as reactivity  decreases  moving down Group VII.
 • The atomic mass also  increases  moving down the group as subatomic particles are added on.
 • Element Q is thus  more   reactive  than bromine and has a  lower  relative atomic mass.
 A  is incorrect as since Q is more reactive than bromine it must sit above it so its relative atomic mass must be  less  than that of bromine.
 C  and  D  are incorrect as Q is more reactive than bromine since it  displaced bromine  from KBr.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which diagram shows an alloy?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • An alloy is a mixture of metals or metals and non-metals that have been mixed together for a purpose.
 • They are not chemically combined.
 B  is incorrect as this shows two elements that are not mixed.
 C  is incorrect as this shows a regular pattern of atoms; alloys contain elements with different sized atoms that distort this regular pattern.
 D  is incorrect as this shows an element.

 • They are able to conduct heat and electricity due to delocalised electrons.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Compound Y is thermally decomposed with carbon using the apparatus below:
  A brown solid is formed in the reaction tube and the limewater turns cloudy.
 What is compound Y?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • The limewater water has turned cloudy, this shows that a reaction has taken place and that carbon dioxide has been produced.
 • Metals that are below carbon in the reactivity series are reduced with carbon. The only metal in the list above that is below carbon in the reactivity series is copper. The equation is:
 • 2 CuO + C → 2 Cu + CO 2
 B, C  and  D  are incorrect as they are all more reactive metals than carbon, so carbon will not reduce them.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
In a blast furnace, iron (III) oxide is converted into iron and carbon monoxide is converted into carbon dioxide, as shown in the equation:
 Fe 2 O 3   + 3CO → 2 Fe + 3 CO 2
 What happens to each of these reactants?
options: A. Iron (III) oxide is reduced and carbon monoxide is oxidised.
B. Iron (III) oxide is oxidised and carbon monoxide is reduced.
C. Both iron (III) oxide and carbon monoxide are oxidised.
D. Both iron (III) oxide and carbon monoxide are reduced.
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because
 • The carbon monoxide is  oxidised  as it gains oxygen:
 • 3CO → 3CO 2
 • Iron (III) oxide is  reduced  as it loses oxygen:
 • Fe 2 O 3  → 2Fe
 B  is incorrect as carbon monoxide is oxidised, oxygen is added to make it carbon dioxide and iron (III) oxide is reduced as oxygen is removed.
 C  is incorrect as iron (III) oxide is reduced as oxygen is removed
 D  is incorrect as carbon monoxide is oxidised; oxygen is added to make it carbon dioxide.

 • Iron is found as an oxide in the ore haematite as the compound Fe 2 O 3
 • Iron is less reactive than carbon and can be extracted in a blast furnace. So electrolysis is not used to extract it from its ore.
 • Iron is used to make cooking utensils when made into the alloy stainless steel.
 A  and  C  are incorrect as iron is extracted using displacement in a blast furnace as it is less reactive than carbon.
 D  is incorrect as iron can be made into the alloy stainless steel, which gives it the properties needed to make cooking utensils

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:

 | filtration

 | chlorination
 | distillation
 |

 | filtration
 | distillation
 |
 | D
 | filtration
 | chlorination
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • After the settling stage, filtration is used to remove any  insoluble solids  such as sand and organic matter.
 • Once filtration is complete, chlorination is performed which kills any  bacteria  present.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Four chemical processes are described below. Which reactions contribute to global warming?
 | 1
 | Reacting hydrochloric acid with magnesium carbonate.
 |
 | 2
 | The complete combustion of propane.
 |
 | 3
 | Heating calcium carbonate.
 |
 | 4
 | Reacting sodium hydroxide with magnesium carbonate.
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because
 • Reactions 1, 2 and 3 all produce  carbon dioxide  which is a Greenhouse Gas and contributes to global warming:
 • Reaction 1: MgCO 3  + 2HCl → MgCl 2  + H 2 O +  CO 2
 • Reaction 2: C 3 H 8  +5O 2  →  3CO 2   + 4H 2 O
 • Reaction 3: CaCO 3  → CaO +  CO 2
 B, C and D are incorrect as reacting sodium hydroxide and magnesium carbonate would not produce CO 2  as carbonates are alkaline substances, so will not react with other alkalis.

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which row correctly shows two ways of reducing the formation of acid rain?
 | A
 | Use a catalytic convertor
 | Reduce the amount of livestock farming
 |
 | B
 | Plant more trees
 | Use fuels containing low levels of sulfur
 |
 | C
 | Use fuels containing low levels of sulfur
 | Use a catalytic convertor
 |
 | D
 | Reduce the amount of livestock farming
 | Plant more trees
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • When fuels containing sulfur are burnt, they emit sulfur dioxide
 • Acid rain is caused by sulfur dioxide
 • Reducing the emissions of sulfur dioxide will reduce the amount of acid rain formed
 • Oxides of nitrogen are formed in a car engine
 • Catalytic convertors remove the oxides of nitrogen which causes acid rain
 • Reducing the emissions of the oxides of nitrogen will reduce the amount of acid rain formed
 A ,  B  and  D  are incorrect as planting more trees removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. Reducing the amount of livestock farming decreases methane emissions. Carbon dioxide and methane are both greenhouse gases that cause climate change

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Flue gas desulfurisation uses calcium oxide to reduce the emissions of sulfur dioxide.
 Which statements are correct?
 | 1
 | Sulfur dioxide is a basic oxide
 |
 | 2
 | Sulfur dioxide is responsible for the production of acid rain 
 |
 | 3
 | Calcium oxide reacts with acids
 |
 | 4
 | Sulfur dioxide emissions can also be reduced by using low sulfur fuels
 |
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • 1 is incorrect as sulfur will form an acidic oxide because sulfur is a non-metal
 • 2 is correct as sulfur dioxide will dissolve in rain to form acid rain
 • 3 is correct as calcium oxide is a basic oxide so will react with acids to form a salt and water
 • 4 is correct as when fuels containing sulfur burn, they produce sulfur dioxide
 • The less sulfur the fuel contains, the less sulfur dioxide they emit when burned

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The first three members of a homologous series are shown.
  Why do these molecules represent a homologous series?
options: A. They contain carbon and hydrogen atoms.
C. They have the same functional group.
D. They react differently from each other.
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • A homologous series is a family of chemicals with  similar properties  that share the same general formula and which have the same  functional group .
 • Each atom in the series has an oxygen atom with a double bond to a carbon. This is a series called  aldehydes.  This is not a group that you need to be able to draw or recall, but you must be able to look at a structure and see the pattern in a series and recognise it as a functional group.
 A  is incorrect as this would be the definition of a  hydrocarbon
 B  is incorrect as the molecules shown have saturated carbon-carbon bonds, but this does not make a homologous series.
 D  is incorrect as a homologous series will have similar chemical properties.

 substance Y + steam    ethanol

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:

set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:

 Which temperature could be the melting point of a pure sample of the substance?
set-1/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because
 • The substance is a  solid  at room temperature which is 20  °C.
 • Its melting point must be above this temperature but must also be a  specific  number and  not a range  as the question states that the substance is pure.
 A  is incorrect as its melting point must be  above  room temperature so it has to be above 20 °C.
 B  and  C  are incorrect as pure substances boil at a  specific  temperature so their melting point would also be a specific temperature i.e. not a range of temperatures.

 [2]
set-1/paper-3-theory-core.explanation:
The evidence for each of the following is:

 • (Particle  A  has the) same number of protons and electrons;  [1 mark]

 • Make sure you are aware of the difference between an atom, isotope and ion in terms of subatomic particles
 • Atoms of the same element have the same number of protons and electrons
 • Isotopes of the same element have different numbers of neutrons but the same number of protons
 • Ions of the same element have different numbers of electrons but the same number of protons

 • Physical change 2: Water vapour / steam to water = condensing

set-1/paper-3-theory-core.stem:

set-1/paper-3-theory-core.explanation:

 • Sulfur dioxide;  [1 mark]
 • (Formed by) burning fossil fuels containing sulfur / volcanoes;  [1 mark]
 • Nitrogen dioxide;  [1 mark]

 • At high temperatures;  [1 mark]    Not exhaust

 • When combustion of a fuel containing sulfur impurities occurs, sulfur dioxide is formed

 |

 • The particles cannot move in a solid but they do  vibrate.
 A  is incorrect as particles in a solid cannot move as described in statement 1.
 C  is incorrect as particles in a solid cannot move as described in statements 1 and 3
 D  is incorrect as statement 4 also applies to particles in a solid.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The rate of diffusion of two gases, methane, CH 4 , and propene, C 3 H 6 , is measured using the apparatus shown.
  Which gas diffuses at a faster rate and why?
 |  
 | Fastest gas
 | Reason
 |
 | A
 | Propene
 | Propene molecules are heavier and so move faster.
 |
 | B
 | Methane
 | Methane is a lighter molecule.
 |
 | C
 | Propene
 | Propene is unsaturated so is more reactive.
 |
 | D
 | Methane
 | Methane molecules are smaller so fit through the hole more easily.
 |
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • The rate of diffusion of a gas depends on its  relative molecular mass .
 • The  M r  of methane is 16 g/mole whereas the  M r  of propene is 42 g/mole.
 • Methane is  lighter  and thus diffuses  faster .
 A  is incorrect as propene is heavier than methane so the molecules move  more slowly
 C  is incorrect as the reactivity of propene is irrelevant in this experiment as diffusion is a physical process.
 D  is incorrect as both molecules can fit through the hole.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Calcium reacts with fluorine to form calcium fluoride
 Which statement describes what happens to calcium atoms in this reaction?
options: A. Calcium ions lose electrons to form positive charges. .
B. Calcium atoms gain 3 electrons to form positive ions.
Calcium ions gain 2 electrons to form positive ions.
D. Calcium atoms lose 2 electrons to form positive ions.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because 
 • calcium atoms have  20 electrons , with two electrons in its outermost shell. It  loses  these  two  electrons to form a 2 +  positive ion.
 A  is incorrect as calcium ions do not lose electrons, calcium atoms do.
 B  and  C  are incorrect as calcium atoms need to  lose  2 electrons to form positive ions.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Which of the following statements about graphite and diamond are incorrect?
 | 1
 | They are allotropes of carbon.
 |
 | 2
 | They both conduct electricity.
 |
 | 3
 | They form different numbers of bonds within their structures.
 |
 | 4
 | They have different uses.
 |
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Graphite can conduct electricity as it has  delocalised electrons  that can move and carry charge.
 • In diamond all of the outer shell electrons in the carbon atoms are used in bonding so it does not conduct electricity as there are no free electrons.
 A, C  and  D  are incorrect as these properties are true for both graphite and diamond.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The following statements describe the structure and properties of silicon(IV) oxide.
 • Giant covalent structure held together by many strong covalent bonds.
 • It is a very hard substance.
 Which of the following is correct for statements 1 and 2?
options: A. Statement 2 is correct but statement 1 is incorrect.
C. Both are correct and statement 1 explains statement 2.
D. Both are correct and statement 2 explains statement 1.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Silicon(IV) oxide is the giant molecular compound SiO 2 .
 • Like diamond, silicon dioxide has a  large number  of strong covalent bonds in its structure so it is  very   hard  and has a very  high   melting  point and  boiling  point
 • Both statements are correct and the hardness of SiO 2  comes from its giant molecular structure, hence  C  is correct.
 A ,  B  and  D  are incorrect as these options are not correct for statements 1 and 2.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Ammonia is manufactured by the reaction of hydrogen and nitrogen in the Haber process, as shown in the equation below:
 N 2  + 3 H 2  → 2 NH 3
 16.8 tonnes of ammonia can be produced from 14 tonnes of nitrogen.
 How much nitrogen is needed to produce 51 tonnes of ammonia?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because
 | Step
 | Working out
 |
 | 1
 | The ratio of N 2  : NH 3  is  14 : 16.8. Divide across by the smallest number (14) to find the simplest  ratio .
 | The ratio of N 2  : NH 3  is   1 : 1.2.
 So for every 1 tonne of nitrogen,  1.2  tonnes of ammonia are produced.
 |
 | 2
 | Divide the amount of NH 3  desired (51 tonnes) by 1.2 to calculate the amount of nitrogen required.
 | 
 |
 B ,  C  and  D  are incorrect as these options do not give the correct amount.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The structure of four particles is described in the table.

 What are the correct values for X, Y and Z?

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Lithium has  4 neutrons  as can be read from the Periodic Table.
 • The atomic number of fluorine is  9  so it has 9 protons.
 • The fluoride ion has  one negative  charge so it must have gained one more electron, so it has 9 + 1 =  10  electrons.
 A, B  and  D  are incorrect as these options do not correctly describe each particle .

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: What is the concentration in mol dm -3  of a solution of sodium hydroxide that contains 16 g of NaOH in 200 cm 3  of distilled water?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A :
 | Step
 | Working out
 |
 | 1
 | Calculate moles of NaOH present in the solution.
 | M r  of NaOH = 40
 n  NaOH = 16 ÷ 40 =  0.4
 |
 | 2
 | Divide volume of solution by 1000 to convert to dm 3 .
 | 200 ÷ 1000 =  0.2   dm 3
 |
 | 3
 | Calculate the concentration in moles using c =  n  ÷ V
 | c   = 0.4 ÷ 0.2 =  2   mol dm -3  
 |
 B ,  C  and  D  are incorrect as these options do not give the correct value for the concentration.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Calcium carbide and water react to produce ethyne and calcium hydroxide.
 CaC 2  (s) + 2H 2 O (l) → C 2 H 2  (g) + Ca(OH) 2  (s)
 What is the volume of C 2 H 2  produced, at standard temperature and pressure, when 45 g of water reacts completely with calcium carbide?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B because:
 • One mole of gas at RTP (room temperature and pressure) occupies a volume of 24 dm 3
 • To determine the volume of a gas produced, in this case ethyne, the following equation is used:
 • volume of gas= number of moles of gas x 24 dm 3
 • The number of moles of water is found using     =   = 2.5 mol 
 • Two moles of water produce one mole of ethyne
 • So, the number of moles of ethyne is   = 1.25 mol 
 • Therefore, the volume of gas produced is 1.25 x 24 = 30 dm 3
 A ,  C  and  D  are incorrect as these options do not give the correct volume.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Dilute sulfuric acid is electrolysed using inert electrodes. 
 What are the products of this electrolysis?
 |  
 | cathode
 | anode
 |
 | A
 | oxygen
 | sulfur 
 |
 | B
 | hydrogen
 | sulfur dioxide
 |
 | C
 | oxygen
 | hydrogen
 |
 | D
 | hydrogen
 | oxygen
 |
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • The ions present in sulfuric acid are H +  and SO 4 2-
 • The ions present in water are H +  and OH - 
 • The positive hydrogen ions are attracted to the cathode (negative electrode) where they gain electrons to form hydrogen gas 
 2H +   +   2e -     ⟶   H 2
 • At the anode, oxygen is produced unless a halide ion is present in which case a halogen is produced 
 4OH –     ⟶    O 2    +   2H 2 O   +   4e –
 A  is incorrect as the oxygen is made at the anode, not the cathode and sulfur is not made at the anode
 B  is incorrect as sulfur is not produced at the anode
 C  is incorrect as the products are correct but they have been formed at the incorrect electrode

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which metal could  not  be used for electroplating by using an aqueous solution?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
  •  In electrolysis of aqueous solutions only one type of ion can be discharged at each electrode.
 • The H +  and OH -  ions produced by the dissociation of water in aqueous solutions compete with the other ions in solution.
 • At the cathode , the  more reactive  a metal is the  more it tends to remain as ions  in solution.
 • For electroplating to take place, the metal which is being used as the  coating  must be  unreactive.
 • Sodium could not be used for this purpose as it is too reactive.
 A, B  and  C  are incorrect as they could all be used as these metals are unreactive and are commonly used for electroplating.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: In all chemical reactions, bonds in the reactant species are broken and new bonds are formed in the products. Which statement is correct?
options: A. Bond breaking requires energy and is thus an exothermic process.
Bond breaking requires energy and is thus an endothermic process.
C. Bond breaking releases energy and is thus an exothermic process.
D. Bond breaking releases energy and is thus an endothermic process.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Energy is  required  to break a chemical bond
 • The energy is  absorbed  from the surroundings, hence it is an  endothermic  process.
 A  is incorrect as exothermic processes release energy into the surroundings.
 C  and  D  are incorrect as bond breaking requires energy as it is an endothermic process.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A student was investigating the rate of reaction between iron and a solution of sulfuric acid. Two experiments were performed, P and Q, in which the volume of hydrogen was recorded at regular intervals.
  Which change could explain the difference in results between P and Q?
options: A. The student added a catalyst in P.
B. Larger pieces of iron were used in P.
C. Less concentrated acid was used in P.
D. Larger quantities of both reactants are used P.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  
 • The  steeper  curve in  P  indicates that this reaction has occurred  faster  than  Q  as a higher volume of hydrogen gas is produced in a  shorter  period of time.
 • The addition of a  catalyst  would  speed  up the rate of a reaction and explain why the product is formed faster in  P  than in  Q .
 B  and  C  are incorrect as using larger pieces of Fe and a less concentrated acid would  slow  the reaction down so curve  P  would be  below curve   Q , not above it.
 D  is incorrect as both curves level off at the  same height , indicating the same amount of product is formed in both reactions.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which graph correctly shows the effect of increasing the temperature on the rate of reaction between magnesium and sulfuric acid in which neither reactant runs out?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  
 • Increasing the reaction temperature increases the rate of reaction so the correct graph should show a  continuous   increase  in rate which is directly related to an increasing temperature.
 B  is incorrect as it shows a levelling off of the rate even though the temperature continues to increase.
 C  is incorrect as the shape of the graph indicates that the rate has decreased dramatically with an increasing temperature.
 D  is incorrect as it shows a decrease in rate as the temperature increases.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A student reacts a metal carbonate with nitric acid and measures the volume of carbon dioxide gas released at regular intervals. The results of the experiment are shown in the graph.
  Between which two measurements was the reaction the fastest?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  
 • The line of the graph is at its  steepest  between 4 and 6 minutes.
 • This indicates that a  larger volume of gas  was being produced in a  shorter time  than at any other point during the reaction.
 A ,  B  and  D  are incorrect as these sections of the graph are not as steep as the section between 4 and 6 minutes.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The reaction for the production of ammonia is shown below.
 N 2 (g) + 3H 2 (g)    2NH 3 (g)
 What is the effect of increasing pressure on the rate of production of ammonia and the percentage yield of ammonia?
 |  
 | rate of production
 | percentage yield
 |
 | A
 | increases
 | decreases
 |
 | B
 | increases
 | increases
 |
 | C
 | decreases
 | increases
 |
 | D
 | decreases
 | decreases
 |
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  
 • From the balanced equation there are  4 moles  of gaseous reactants to  2 moles  of gaseous product.
 • An increase in pressure would shift the equilibrium to the side with  less  gaseous moles, favouring the  forward reaction.
 • Therefore the percentage yield of ammonia  increases.
 A  is incorrect as the percentage yield increases with increasing pressure.
 C  and  D  are incorrect as the rate if production increases with increasing pressure.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Three reactions are shown below.
 • NO + O 3  → NO 2  + O 2
 • 2C + O 2  → 2CO
 • 2MgO + O 2  → 2MgO 2
 Which row correctly describes the process each reactant molecule undergoes?
 |  
 | NO
 | O 3
 | MgO
 |
 | A
 | oxidised
 | reduced
 | oxidised
 |
 | B
 | oxidised
 | oxidised
 | reduced
 |
 | C
 | reduced
 | oxidised
 | oxidised
 |
 | D
 | reduced
 | reduced
 | oxidised
 |
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  
 • For NO and MgO, oxygen has been added so they are  oxidised :
 NO → NO 2             MgO → MgO 2
 • For O 3 , oxygen has been removed so it has been  reduced :
 O 3  → O 2
 B ,  C  and  D  are incorrect as these options do not correctly describe what happens to each reactant molecule.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Most insect bites cause a stinging sensation because of the injection of a weak acid into the surface of the skin. Which substance could be used to neutralise the acid from an insect bite?
 |  
 | substance
 | pH
 |
 | A
 | battery acid
 | 1
 |
 | B
 | toothpaste
 | 8
 |
 | C
 | grill cleaner
 | 13
 |
 | D
 | lime juice
 | 3
 |
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  
 • Weak acids are neutralised by  weak   bases .
 • Toothpaste has a pH of 8 and is the safest option as it won't harm skin which is  pH neutral .
 A  and  D  are incorrect as these are  acidic substances  and will only further aggravate the problem.
 C  is incorrect as grill cleaner is  too abrasive  due to its high pH.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A student is provided with an unmarked beaker containing a colourless solution and asked to identify it. The student decides to perform a series of reactions with the solution and record the observations.
 Which of these observations is not indicative of an acid?
options: A. The solution causes blue litmus to turn red.
B. On heating and the addition of copper oxide, the solution turns blue.
C. On the addition of ammonium carbonate, a colourless, pungent gas is released.
D. On the addition of a piece of magnesium, effervescence was produced and the magnesium piece ‘disappeared’ after a few minutes.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  
 • Ammonium carbonate reacts with  alkalis  to produce the metal carbonate, ammonia gas and water. Ammonia gas is  colourless  and  pungent
 • An example is the reaction with sodium hydroxide:
 • (NH 4 ) 2 CO 3  + 2NaOH → Na 2 CO 3  + 2H 2 O + 2NH 3
 • The reaction is  not characteristic  of an acid as an acid-base neutralisation reaction produces a salt and water only.
 A  is incorrect as acids have pH values of  below 7  and will turn blue litmus paper  red .
 B  is incorrect as copper oxide is a weak base and will react with an acid forming  blue  hydrated copper salt. For example with sulfuric acid: 
 CuO +H 2 SO 4  → CuSO 4  + H 2 O
 D  is incorrect as magnesium reacts with acids producing the metal salt and  bubbles  of hydrogen gas. For example with hydrochloric acid:  
 Mg + 2HCl → MgCl 2  + H 2

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Bromine and rubidium react together to form the compound rubidium bromide. Which row correctly describes the formula and colour of rubidium bromide?
 |  
 | formula
 | colour
 |
 | A
 | RbBr
 | dark grey
 |
 | B
 | RbBr 2
 | dark grey
 |
 | C
 | RbBr
 | white
 |
 | D
 | RbBr 2
 | white
 |
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  
 • Rubidium is a  Group I  metal which loses its  single outer shell electron , forming positively charged ions, Rb + .
 • Bromine is a  Group VII  halogen which requires just  one electron  to complete its outer  shell, forming the negatively charged ion Br - .
 • Both ions attract in a 1:1 ratio forming the ionic compound  RbBr .
 • The salts of the metals in Group I, II and III are generally  white solids , hence RbBr is white.
 A  and  B  are incorrect as the compound formed is a white solid.
 D  is incorrect as the formula for rubidium bromide is RbBr.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Astatine is a radioactive Group VII element which is extremely unstable, making it difficult to study. The physical and chemical properties of astatine can only be estimated.
 Which row most likely describes the properties of astatine?
 |  
 | State
 | Colour
 | Reaction with KI (aq)
 |
 | A
 | liquid
 | yellow
 | brown colour
 |
 | B
 | solid
 | green
 | no reaction
 |
 | C
 | gas
 | dark brown
 | brown colour
 |
 | D
 | solid
 | black
 | no reaction
 |
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  
 • The physical state of astatine is most likely  solid  as the melting points and boiling points  increase  moving down as the atomic number increases.
 • The colour is most likely  black  as the colour darkens moving down Group VII.
 • It is unlikely to be able to displace iodine as iodine is above astatine in the group and reactivity in Group VII  increases  as you  move up  the group.
 A  and  C  are incorrect as astatine is more than likely to be a  solid .
 B  is incorrect as the colour of astatine is likely to be  black  or a very  dark grey .

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A solution of a lithium halide and a halogen are mixed together. A reaction occurs and the mixture darkens in colour.
 What is present in the reaction mixture?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C
 • In Group VII reactivity decreases moving down the group and the atomic radius increases, so the outer shell gets further from the nucleus.
 • The attraction between the nucleus and electrons gets weaker, so an electron is less easily gained, making it more difficult for the halogens to receive electrons.
 • For the halogen in solution to displace the halide from the lithium halide, it must sit above the halide
 • Chlorine in above iodine in the Periodic Table so chlorine will displace iodine from lithium iodide to produce lithium chloride and iodine
 • chlorine + lithium iodide → lithium chloride + iodine
 • Aqueous iodine is a brown solution, so as iodine is produced, the reaction mixture will darken
 A  and  B  are incorrect as bromine sits  below  both chlorine and fluorine and cannot displace them as it is less reactive than both.
 D  is incorrect as chlorine sits  below  fluorine.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Astatine is found below iodine in Group 7 of the periodic table.
 What is its formula and state at room temperature?
 |  
 | Formula
 | State at room temperature 
 |
 |  A
 | At
 | gas
 |
 |  B
 | At
 | solid
 |
 |  C
 | At 2
 | liquid
 |
 |  D
 | At 2
 | solid
 |
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  
 • Going down Group 7 the melting and boiling point of the halogens increases
 • The intermolecular forces therefore get stronger and need more energy to break
 • Fluorine and chlorine are both gases, bromine, a liquid, and iodine and astatine solids 
 • Group 7 elements exist as molecules and are diatomic, meaning they go round in pairs

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Brass is an alloy of two metals.
 Which row describes the correct use of the two metals that brass is made from?
 |  
 | metal 1
 | metal 2
 |
 | A
 | galvanising steel
 | making aircraft
 |
 | B
 | electrical wiring
 | galvanising steel
 |
 | C
 | making aircraft
 | making cutlery
 |
 | D
 | making cooking pans
 | electrical wiring
 |
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Brass is an alloy; it is 70% copper and 30% zinc.
 • Copper is used for electrical wiring as it has low resistance which makes it a good conductor of electricity.
 • Zinc is used in galvanising steel as it is more reactive and will oxidise before the steel does (sacrificial protection!).
 A  is incorrect as aircraft are made from aluminium, a metal not found in brass. Aluminum is light which makes it suitable for building airplanes.
 C  is incorrect as aluminium would be used to make aircraft and stainless steel (alloy of carbon) is used to make cutlery.
 D  is incorrect as cooking pans are made from copper as it is a good conductor of heat. Electrical wiring is also made from copper due to its low resistance

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which diagram shows an alloy?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • An alloy is a mixture of metals or metals and non-metals that have been mixed together for a purpose.
 • They are not chemically combined.
 B  is incorrect as this shows two elements that are not mixed.
 C  is incorrect as this shows a regular pattern of atoms; alloys contain elements with different sized atoms that distort this regular pattern.
 D  is incorrect as this shows an element.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Small blocks of zinc are attached to ship hulls which are commonly made from steel, an alloy of iron. This is done to prevent the hull from rusting.
 Which statement explains this process?
options: A. Zinc is higher up on the reactivity series than iron so has a higher tendency to become reduced.
B. Zinc is lower down on the reactivity series than iron so has a higher tendency to become reduced.
C. Zinc is higher up on the reactivity series than iron so has a higher tendency to become oxidised.
D. Zinc is lower down on the reactivity series than iron so has a higher tendency to become oxidised.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Sacrificial rust protection  works by using a metal placed  higher  up on the reactivity series and connecting it to the object that needs to be protected.
 • Zinc is a more reactive metal so is more likely to  lose   electrons  (and become oxidised) than iron and it readily donates its electrons to any iron ions that might have formed, stopping them from corroding.
 • The zinc metal will be  corroded   in   preference  to the steel hull, hence preventing it from rusting.
 A ,  B  and  D  are incorrect as the sacrificial metal must be  above iron  on the reactivity series to be able to oxidise before the iron atoms do.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
In a blast furnace, iron (III) oxide is converted into iron and carbon monoxide is converted into carbon dioxide, as shown in the equation:
 Fe 2 O 3   + 3CO → 2 Fe + 3 CO 2
 What happens to each of these reactants?
options: A. Iron (III) oxide is reduced and carbon monoxide is oxidised.
B. Iron (III) oxide is oxidised and carbon monoxide is reduced.
C. Both iron (III) oxide and carbon monoxide are oxidised.
D. Both iron (III) oxide and carbon monoxide are reduced.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because
 • The carbon monoxide is  oxidised  as it gains oxygen:
 • 3CO → 3CO 2
 • Iron (III) oxide is  reduced  as it loses oxygen:
 • Fe 2 O 3  → 2Fe
 B  is incorrect as carbon monoxide is oxidised, oxygen is added to make it carbon dioxide and iron (III) oxide is reduced as oxygen is removed.
 C  is incorrect as iron (III) oxide is reduced as oxygen is removed
 D  is incorrect as carbon monoxide is oxidised; oxygen is added to make it carbon dioxide.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram shows how aluminium is manufactured by electrolysis.
  What are the anode and cathode made of?
 |  
 | anode
 | cathode
 |
 | A
 | aluminium
 | aluminium
 |
 | B
 | aluminium
 | graphite
 |
 | C
 | graphite
 | aluminium
 |
 | D
 | graphite
 | graphite
 |
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • In the electrolysis of aluminium, both electrodes are made from graphite.
 • Graphite is an allotrope of carbon which is chemically inert and resistant to corrosion but does conduct heat and electricity, so the flow of electricity and heat is maintained while the electrodes do not interfere with the chemistry of the process.
 A, B  and  C  are incorrect as aluminium is a metal which has different properties than graphite and would participate in the chemistry of the process and hence interrupt the extraction.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Reactions of three metals and their oxides are shown in the table.
 | metal
 | reacts with cold water
 | metal oxide reacts with carbon
 |
 | P
 | no
 | no
 |
 | Q
 | no
 | yes
 |
 | R
 | yes
 | no
 |
 What is the order of reactivity of the metals?
 |  
 | Least reactive
 | →
 | Most reactive
 |
 | A
 | P
 | Q
 | R
 |
 | B
 | Q
 | P
 | R
 |
 | C
 | Q
 | R
 | P
 |
 | D
 | R
 | P
 | Q

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Metals that are reactive will react with cold water.
 • A reactive metal oxide is therefore not going to be reactive with carbon, carbon is not going to reduce the metal as carbon is less reactive.
 • Q is the least reactive as it will not react with water and it is lower than carbon in the reactivity series so its oxide will react with carbon.
 • P is the next reactive metal in the reactivity series as it doesn’t react with water and its oxide will not react with carbon so is higher in the reactivity series than carbon.
 • R is the most reactive as it reacts with cold water and its oxide can’t be reduced by carbon.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Tin is less reactive than iron and the metal is extracted from its ore cassiterite, SnO 2 .
 Which of the following statements are correct?
 • Tin does not conduct electricity.
 • Tin is hard and shiny
 • Tn can be extracted from cassiterite using carbon.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Tin is a hard and shiny metal
 • Tin is less reactive than carbon, so carbon can be used to reduce it.
 Statement 1 is incorrect because tin is a metal; metallic bonding in metals has delocalised electrons that allow the metal to conduct electricity.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Which row correctly shows two ways of reducing the formation of acid rain?
 | A
 | Use a catalytic convertor
 | Reduce the amount of livestock farming
 |
 | B
 | Plant more trees
 | Use fuels containing low levels of sulfur
 |
 | C
 | Use fuels containing low levels of sulfur
 | Use a catalytic convertor
 |
 | D
 | Reduce the amount of livestock farming
 | Plant more trees
 |
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • When fuels containing sulfur are burnt, they emit sulfur dioxide
 • Acid rain is caused by sulfur dioxide
 • Reducing the emissions of sulfur dioxide will reduce the amount of acid rain formed
 • Oxides of nitrogen are formed in a car engine
 • Catalytic convertors remove the oxides of nitrogen which causes acid rain
 • Reducing the emissions of the oxides of nitrogen will reduce the amount of acid rain formed
 A ,  B  and  D  are incorrect as planting more trees removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. Reducing the amount of livestock farming decreases methane emissions. Carbon dioxide and methane are both greenhouse gases that cause climate change

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Flue gas desulfurisation uses calcium oxide to reduce the emissions of sulfur dioxide.
 Which statements are correct?
 | 1
 | Sulfur dioxide is a basic oxide
 |
 | 2
 | Sulfur dioxide is responsible for the production of acid rain 
 |
 | 3
 | Calcium oxide reacts with acids
 |
 | 4
 | Sulfur dioxide emissions can also be reduced by using low sulfur fuels
 |
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • 1 is incorrect as sulfur will form an acidic oxide because sulfur is a non-metal
 • 2 is correct as sulfur dioxide will dissolve in rain to form acid rain
 • 3 is correct as calcium oxide is a basic oxide so will react with acids to form a salt and water
 • 4 is correct as when fuels containing sulfur burn, they produce sulfur dioxide
 • The less sulfur the fuel contains, the less sulfur dioxide they emit when burned

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Four chemical processes are described below. Which reactions contribute to global warming?
 | 1
 | Reacting hydrochloric acid with magnesium carbonate.
 |
 | 2
 | The complete combustion of propane.
 |
 | 3
 | Heating calcium carbonate.
 |
 | 4
 | Reacting sodium hydroxide with magnesium carbonate.
 |
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because
 • Reactions 1, 2 and 3 all produce  carbon dioxide  which is a Greenhouse Gas and contributes to global warming:
 • Reaction 1: MgCO 3  + 2HCl → MgCl 2  + H 2 O +  CO 2
 • Reaction 2: C 3 H 8  +5O 2  →  3CO 2   + 4H 2 O
 • Reaction 3: CaCO 3  → CaO +  CO 2
 B, C and D are incorrect as reacting sodium hydroxide and magnesium carbonate would not produce CO 2  as carbonates are alkaline substances, so will not react with other alkalis.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The structures of six organic compounds compound  A  are shown.
  Which two compounds are isomers of one another?
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Isomers have the same molecular formula but different displayed formula 
 • C  and  F  both have the molecular formula C 5 H 12   but their atoms are arranged differently 
 A ,  B  and  D  are incorrect as the compounds do not have the same molecular formula.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

 substance Y + steam    ethanol

 Which row correctly identifies the products of a reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol?

 A, B  and  C  are incorrect as they are not the products from this type of reaction.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which statement about polymers is correct?
options: B. Condensation polymers can all be hydrolysed to give amino acids.
Condensation polymers only exist in nature.
D. Forming addition polymers produces only one product.
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Addition polymerisation occurs in molecules that contain a C=C double bond.
 • The bond breaks and molecules join together to form a much larger molecule.
 • There is no other product formed.
 A  is incorrect as poly(ethene) is an example of an addition polymer and is not biodegradable.
 B  and  C  are incorrect as Terylene is an example of a condensation polymer which cannot be hydrolysed to make amino acids, and is also not a natural polymer.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A student wants to investigate the rate of reaction between marble chips and hydrochloric acid by measuring the volume of carbon dioxide produced with different concentrations of acid.
 The equation for the reaction is as follows:
 2 HCl + MgCO 3  → MgCl 2  + CO 2  + H 2 O
 Which of the following lists of equipment can she use to measure the volume of the gas produced?
options: A. Gas syringe, cotton wool, bung, delivery tube
B. Gas syringe, conical flask, bung, delivery tube
C. Gas syringe, beaker, bung, balance
D. Balloon, conical flask, stopper, balance
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because: 
 • The four pieces of equipment in option B are the correct setup to perform this measurement as shown below.
  A  is incorrect as the cotton wool would allow the gas to  escape .
 C  is incorrect as a beaker cannot be sealed by a bung.
 D  is incorrect as this equipment could not be used to measure gas volume.

set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A student decided to investigate the rate of reaction between marble chips and dilute hydrochloric acid at 35  o C.

 W  a balance
 X  a thermometer

 Z  a stopwatch
 Which pieces of apparatus did she use?
options: A. X ,  Y  and  Z  only
B. W ,  Y  and  Z  only
C. W ,  X  and  Z  only
D. W, X ,  Y  and  Z
set-2/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • The mass of marble chips needs to be controlled so she would need a balance
 • To keep the temperature at 35  o C a thermometer would be needed
 • To measure the volume of hydrochloric acid a measuring cylinder is needed
 • Since this is a rate of reaction investigation, time has to be recorded using a stopwatch or timer

set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
Concentrated ammonia solution gives off ammonia gas. Concentrated hydrochloric acid gives off hydrogen chloride gas. Ammonia, NH 3 , and hydrogen chloride, HCl, are both colourless gases. Ammonia reacts with hydrogen chloride to make the white solid ammonium chloride.
 Apparatus is set up as shown.
  After ten minutes a white solid forms in the tube where the gases meet.
 i) Write the chemical equation for the reaction of ammonia with hydrogen chloride.
 [1]
 ii) Name the process by which the ammonia and hydrogen chloride gases move in the tube.
 [1]
 iii) At which point, A, B, C or D, does the white solid form? Explain why the white solid forms at that point.
 [3]
 iv) The experiment was repeated at a higher temperature. Predict how the results of the experiment would be different. Explain your answer.
 [3]
set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
i)  The chemical equation for the reaction of ammonia with hydrogen chloride is:
 • NH 3  + HCl → NH 4 Cl;  [1 mark]
 ii)  The process by which the ammonia and hydrogen chloride gases move in the tube is:
 • Diffusion;  [1 mark]
 iii)  The point at which the white solid forms and why is:
 • The solid forms at point A;  [1 mark]
 • The ammonia molecules / particles have a smaller mass;  [1 mark]
 • The molecules move/ diffuse faster;  [1 mark]
 iv) How the results of the experiment would be different at a higher temperature:
 • The solid forms in less time/ faster/ quicker;  [1 mark]
 • The particles / molecules have more energy;  [1 mark]
 • The particles move faster/ diffuse faster;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 8 marks]
 • Make sure you know the formula of common molecules like ammonia and hydrogen chloride
 • To get more credit in your answers when talking about diffusion you need to mention both the energy and speed of the particles

set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
Ethylamine, CH 3 –CH 2 –NH 2 , is a base which has similar properties to ammonia.
 In aqueous ethylamine, there is the following equilibrium.
 CH 3 –CH 2 –NH 2  + H 2 O   CH 3 –CH 2 –NH 3 +  + OH –
 Explain why water is behaving as an acid in this reaction.
set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
Water is behaving as an acid as:
 • It is a proton donor;  [1 mark] 
 [Total: 1 mark] 
 • Water is donating one of its protons to the ethylamine 
 • CH 3 –CH 2 –NH 2  +  H 2 O   CH 3 –CH 2 –N H 3 +  + OH –
 • This is why the OH –  ion is formed
 • This makes the solution basic

set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
The table below shows the elements in the second period of the Periodic Table and some of their oxidation states in their most common compounds.
  i) What does it mean when the only oxidation state of an element is zero?
 [1]
 ii) Explain why some elements have positive oxidation states but others have negative ones.
 [2]
 iii) Select two elements in the table which exist as diatomic molecules of the type X 2 .
 [2]
set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
i) When the only oxidation state of an element is zero it means that the element:
 • Does not form compounds / does not accept and does not lose electrons / has a full outer shell / has 8e -  in outer shell / it is a Noble Gas / it is in Group 0/8;  [1 mark]
 ii) Some elements have positive oxidation states but others have negative ones as:
 • Elements with a small number of outer electrons lose electrons and are then positive;  [1 mark]
 • Elements with a large number of outer electrons gain electrons and are then negative;  [1 mark]
 iii)  Two elements in the table which exist as diatomic molecules of the type X 2  are:
 Any  two  from
 • Nitrogen;  [1 mark]
 • Oxygen;  [1 mark]
 • Fluorine;  [1 mark]  Accept symbols / molecular formulae
 [Total: 5 marks]
 • This question is checking your basic redox knowledge by asking questions in  a slightly less direct manner than the normal
 • You are also expected to recall the common diatomic gases, which are useful when writing equations late

set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
Aqueous sodium hydroxide is a base.
 Complete this sentence about the different types of bases. Bases are metal hydroxides or metal _______________________
set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
The completed sentence is:
 • Bases are metal hydroxides or metal  oxides;   [1 mark]
 [Total: 1 mark]

set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
Manganese is a transition element. It has more than one valency and the metal and its compounds are catalysts.
 Predict three other properties of manganese that are typical of transition elements.
set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
Three other properties of transition elements are:
 Any three from:
 • High densities;  [1 mark]
 • High melting point / boiling point;  [1 mark]
 • Form coloured compounds;  [1 mark]
 • Hardness;  [1 mark]
 • Form complex ions;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 3 marks]
 • There are other properties that many metals share, but this is asking you for the properties that are typical of transition elements
 • Stating that they are good electrical conductors would not gain you the mark, as this is a property applicable to all metals

set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
The alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons. They form a homologous series, the members of which have the same chemical properties.
 They undergo addition reactions and are easily oxidised.
 The following hydrocarbons are isomers.
  i) Explain why these two hydrocarbons are isomers.
 [2]
 ii) Give the structural formula of another hydrocarbon which is isomeric with the above.
 [1]
set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
i) These two hydrocarbons are isomers because:
 • Have same molecular formula / both are C 5 H 12 ;  [1 mark]
 • They have different structural formulae / different structures;  [1 mark]
 ii)  The structural formula of another hydrocarbon which is isomeric with the above is:
 • CH 3 -CH 2 -CH=CH-CH 3  / any other correct isomer;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 3 marks]
 • Remember:  The molecular formulae is the actual number of atoms of each element in a compound but the structural formula is how the atoms are arranged
 • In the question, the names of the two isomers are 3-methylbutene and pent-1-ene
 • Their atoms are arranged differently but they both have the same molecular formula of C 5 H 12
 • A quick way of working out another isomer is to simply move the position of the double bond

set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
There are two types of polymerisation, addition and condensation.
 Explain the difference between these two types of polymerisation.
set-2/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
The difference between these two types of polymerisation is:
 • Addition polymerisation forms only one product;  [1 mark]
 • Condensation polymerisation forms the polymer and water / a small molecule;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 2 marks]
 • You need to know the difference between addition and condensation polymerisation
 • Addition polymerisation forms only one product because the carbon=carbon double bond breaks open and attaches to another monomer
 • Condensation polymerisation occurs when certain functional groups are used to form a polymer, which results in a small molecule (often water) being released as a second product

set-2/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.stem:

set-2/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.stem:
The diagram shows the apparatus used to separate a mixture of water, boiling point 100 °C, and ethanol, boiling point 78 °C.

set-2/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.explanation:

 • You should definitely know the label for the tripod from your previous studies
 • Any column / piece of equipment making the distance between the flask and the side-arm (to the condenser) longer is being added to help fractional distillation occur

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Solid P melts at exactly 60 o C and boils at exactly 310 o C. Solid Q dissolves in ethanol and shows a green colour and a yellow colour when analysed using paper chromatography.
 Which row is correct?
 |  
 | Contains only one substance
 | Contains more than one substance

 | Q

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Impure substances have melting points and boiling points that fall in a  range of  temperatures  while pure substances have  exact  and  sharp  melting and boiling  points.
 • Solid P has an  exact  melting point and boiling point hence it is a pure substance.
 • Paper chromatography of solid Q produces two spots, indicating it must contain more than one substance.
 A  and  B  are incorrect as solid Q contains  more than one  substance.
 C  is incorrect as solid P contains only  one  substance.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Element X contains 12 of each sub-atomic particle.
 What is the correct Group number for element X?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Element X contains 12 of each sub-atomic particle means that it contains 12 protons, 12 neutrons and 12 electrons
 • 12 protons mean an atomic number of 12, which is the Group 2 metal magnesium
 • 12 protons and 12 neutrons mean a mass number of 24, which is the Group 2 metal magnesium
 • 12 electrons mean an electronic configuration of 2,8,2
 • This means that the element is in Period 3 
 • It contains 2 outer electrons, which means that it is in Group 2
 • The element that is in Period 3 and Group 2 is magnesium
 A ,  B  and  C  are incorrect as element X is magnesium which belongs to Group II

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Copper is sometimes used to make cooking utensils and pans.
 Three properties of copper are shown below:
 | 1
 | Good conductor of electricity.
 |
 | 2
 | Corrosion resistant.
 |
 | 3
 | Good conductor of heat.
 |
 Which of these properties make it good for making cooking utensils?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Cooking utensils are exposed to water and other substances so they need to be very resistant to corrosion.
 • Cooking utensils such as pans need to be good conductors of heat to transfer the heat energy to the food.
 • Copper is resistant to corrosion and a good conductor of heat.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Calcium reacts with fluorine to form calcium fluoride
 Which statement describes what happens to calcium atoms in this reaction?
options: A. Calcium ions lose electrons to form positive charges. .
B. Calcium atoms gain 3 electrons to form positive ions.
Calcium ions gain 2 electrons to form positive ions.
D. Calcium atoms lose 2 electrons to form positive ions.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because 
 • calcium atoms have  20 electrons , with two electrons in its outermost shell. It  loses  these  two  electrons to form a 2 +  positive ion.
 A  is incorrect as calcium ions do not lose electrons, calcium atoms do.
 B  and  C  are incorrect as calcium atoms need to  lose  2 electrons to form positive ions.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: The atom of element Z has 6 electrons in its outer shell. How would this element react?
options: A. It shares two electrons with four from another atom to form two covalent bonds
B. It shares four electrons with four from another atom to form four covalent bonds
C. It shares four electrons with two from another atom to form two covalent bonds
D. It shares two electrons with two from another atom to form two covalent bonds
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Element Z is a  Group 6  element since it has 6 electrons in its outer shell.
 • Group  6  elements are nonmetals and metalloids that form covalent bonds by sharing electrons.
 • By sharing  2  electrons with  2  from another atom it achieves a full outer shell configuration.
 A ,  B  and  C  are incorrect as the combinations in these formulae do not provide a full outer shell for each atom.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which statement correctly describes the structure of macromolecules?
options: A. Giant molecular crystal which is held together by weak intermolecular forces.
B. Giant molecular crystal which is held together by strong ionic bonds.
C. Giant molecular crystal which is held together by weak metallic bonds.
D. Giant molecular crystal which is held together by strong covalent bonds.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Macromolecular structures form giant crystals.
 • All the atoms in the structure are linked to each other by  strong covalent  bonds.
 • The atoms are joined to each other forming a  regular arrangement .
 A  is incorrect as intermolecular forces are not present within the crystal structure.
 B  and  C  are incorrect as macromolecules are covalently bonded.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: What is the balanced equation for the reaction of methane and oxygen?
options: A. CH 4 (g) + 2 O 2 (g) → CO 2 (g) + H 2 O(g)
B. CH 4 (g) + O 2 (g) → CO 2 (g) + 2 H 2 O(g)
D. CH 4 (g) + 2 O 2 (g) → CO 2 (g) + 2 H 2 O(g)
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 | Step
 | Working out
 |

 | The number of each atom on either side of the reaction  without coefficients  is shown.
 | CH 4 (g) + O 2 (g) → CO 2 (g) + H 2 O(g)

 H x 4
 O x 2
 | C x 1
 H x 2
 O x 3
 |
 |
 | 2
 | There are  equal  numbers of C but  unequal  numbers of H and O on either side. Change the numbers of H and O to match by adjusting the  coefficients .
 | CH 4 (g) +  2  O 2 (g) → CO 2 (g) +  2  H 2 O(g)
 | C x 1
 H x 4
 O x  4
 | C x 1
 H x  4
 O x  4
 |
 |
 A ,  B  and  C  are incorrect as these options do not provide the correct balanced equation.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: What is the oxidation state of Fe in Fe 2 O 3 ?
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  
 • Oxidation number refers to a single  atom  or  ion  which can be on their own or in a compound.
 • The oxidation number of a compound is  0  and of an element is also  0 .
 • The oxidation number of an ion is equal to the  charge  of that ion e.g. F ー  is  -1.
 • The oxidation number of  oxygen  in a compound is always  -2  (except in peroxide R-O-O-R, where it is  -1 ).
 • There are 3 oxygens in Fe 2 O 3 ,  so 3 x -2 = -6.
 • As it is a compound, the overall charge must be 0, hence each Fe atom must be +3 since 2 x 3 = 6  and +6 - 6 = 0.
 A ,  B  and  C  are incorrect as these options do not provide an oxidation number of 0 for the compound.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:

 • Bromide ions produce a cream precipitate with acidified silver nitrate as insoluble silver bromide is formed
 • Iron(III) ions produce a red-brown precipitate when aqueous sodium hydroxide is added
 A  is incorrect as iron(II) ions produce a green precipitate with aqueous sodium hydroxide
 C  is incorrect as iron(II) ions produce a green precipitate with aqueous sodium hydroxide and chloride ions produce a white precipitate with acidified silver nitrate
 D  is incorrect as chloride ions produce a white precipitate with acidified silver nitrate

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A student gradually added excess potassium hydroxide from a burette to a conical flask containing sulfuric acid as part of a rate of reaction investigation.
 Which statement describes the change in pH of the sulfuric acid as the aqueous potassium hydroxide was added?
options: A. The pH decreases from 14 to neutrality and remains constant
B. The pH decreases from 12 to 2
C. The pH increases from 1 to neutrality and remains constant
D. The pH increases from 1 to around 13
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  
 • Potassium hydroxide is a  strong base  and reacts with sulfuric acid to produce salt and water:
 • 2 KOH + H 2 SO 4  → K 2 SO 4  + 2 H 2 O
 • At the beginning of the reaction and before any alkali has been added the pH of the sulfuric acid is 1.
 • As the alkali is added and neutralisation begins, more and more of the acid is neutralised as the alkali is added and the pH rises.
 • As the alkali is added in  excess , the pH continues to rise until it reaches pH 14 which indicates a  strong alkaline  solution.
 A  and  B  are   incorrect as the pH of the acid increases from 1 to 14 as more alkali is added
 C  is incorrect as if the alkali is added in excess then the pH increases beyond neutrality

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Copper(II) sulfate can be prepared by reacting solid copper(II) carbonate with hot sulfuric acid. The copper(II) carbonate is always added in excess.
 Why is the solid reactant added in excess?
options: A. To ensure all of the acid reacts.
B. To make the reaction go faster.
C. To ensure all of the solid reactant has reacted.
D. To increase the product yield.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  
 • Copper(II) carbonate reacts with sulfuric acid to produce copper(II) sulfate:
 • CuCO 3  + H 2 SO 4 → CuSO 4  + H 2 O + CO 2
 • Copper(II) sulfate is  soluble  and is separated from the mixture by  evaporation .
 • If there is any acid remaining in the solution it would become dangerously concentrated during this phase of the preparation.
 • For this reason the carbonate is added in excess to make sure that all of the acid has reacted.
 B  and  D  are incorrect as the rate of reaction and yield are not dependent on there being an excess of only one of the reactants.
 C  is incorrect as any unreacted copper(II) carbonate is removed by  filtration .

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Potassium and krypton are elements in Period 4. Potassium is at the beginning of the period and is more metallic than krypton which is at the end of the period.
 What makes potassium more metallic than krypton?
options: A. It has less electrons than krypton.
B. It has less protons than krypton.
C. It has less electron shells.
D. It has less outer shell electrons.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  
 • The change in metallic to non-metallic character as we move across the Periodic table from left to right is linked to the  electronic configuration  of the elements.
 • Non-metals have  more electrons  in their outer shells than metals.
 • Potassium is in  Group I  and has  1  electron in its outer shell whereas krypton is in  Group VIII  and has  8  electrons in its outer shell.
 A  and  B  are incorrect as although potassium has fewer electrons and protons than krypton, it is the  outer shell electrons  that determine its chemical properties.
 C  is incorrect as both elements are in the same period they have the same number of electron shells.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
An element has an electronic configuration of 2,8,6.
