 • The number of electrons in the outer shell correlates to the group number 
 • 2,8, 6  shows there are six electrons in the outer shell so the element is in Group 6 
 • The period number refers to the number of shells an atom has
 • The number of notations shows the number of shells
 • 2,8,6 has three notations so the element has three shells and is in Period 3

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Metals do not form acidic oxides,  metal   oxides  have  basic  properties. So Q is not a metal.
 • All the other elements are metals
 • P  has a high density and is  ductile  (can be drawn into wires)
 • R  acts as a catalyst; many of the transition metals are used as catalysts in reactions. It also forms an oxide that reacts with acids so has basic properties.
 • S  is a solid used to make alloys. Alloys are metallic mixtures of two or more metals or a metal and a nonmetal.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The reactivity of the halogens decreases moving down the group.
 Which statement explains this observation?
options: A. Decreasing distance between the nucleus and outer shell makes it easier for the atom to attract electrons.
B. Increasing distance between the nucleus and outer shell makes it easier for the atom to attract electrons.
C. Decreasing distance between the nucleus and outer shell makes it harder for the atom to attract electrons.
D. Increasing distance between the nucleus and outer shell makes it harder for the atom to attract electrons.
set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  
 • The Group I elements are  metals  and  lose  their outer shell electron whereas the Group VII elements are nonmetals and need to  gain  just one more electron to achieve an octet (and full outer shell).
 • The atomic radius  increases  moving down the group so the outer shell gets  further   away  from the nucleus the further down you go.
 • The attraction between the nucleus and electrons gets weaker, so an electron is   less   easily   gained  as there is  greater shielding  of the nucleus.
 A  and  C  are incorrect as the distance between the nucleus and outermost shell  increases  moving down the group.
 B  is incorrect as the longer distance makes it  harder  to remove the valence electrons, not harder.

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:

set-3/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Petroleum (crude oil) is a mixture of different hydrocarbons with different chain lengths and physical properties.
 • Petroleum is separated through  fractional distillation , which separates the molecules with similar boiling points called fractions.
 • The fractions have a boiling point range; the boiling point depends on the molecular mass of the molecules.
 • The  larger  the molecular  mass  the  higher  the  boiling   point ; therefore larger molecules with high boiling points are separated at the bottom of the column.
 • The shorter, lighter chains are separated at the top of the column.
 A, C  and  D   are incorrect because chemical reactivity and solubility in water does vary with each fraction but these properties are not used to separate the mixture into fractions.

 • I or At;  [1 mark]
 iv) The element that is in Group V and Period 4 is:
 • As;  [1 mark]
 v) The element that is an unreactive gas used to fill lamps is:

 [Total: 5 marks]
 • Potassium is at the top of the reactivity series with sodium second, showing that the Group I metals are the most reactive of the metals
 • The reactivity of Group I metals increase as you down the group so the Group I metal at the bottom of the group will be the most reactive element

set-3/paper-3-theory-core.stem:

 Solid iodine:
 Iodine gas:
set-3/paper-3-theory-core.explanation:
The separation between the molecules and the type of motion of the molecules is:
 Solid iodine:
 • Separation: the particles are touching / close together;  [1 mark]
 • Motion: The particles are (only) vibrating / are not moving from place to place;  [1 mark]
 Iodine gas:
 • Separation: the particles are far apart;  [1 mark]
 • Motion: the particles are moving fast / randomly / in any direction;  [1 mark]

 • Separation is about the closeness of the particles / the space between the particles
 • Motion is about the movement, which means that you can comment on the type, speed and direction of movement

 • e.g. Gases are more suited to speed and direction of movement as they move rapidly and randomly in all directions

set-3/paper-3-theory-core.stem:

 • 12 protons and 12 neutrons mean a mass number of 24, which is the Group 2 metal magnesium
 • 12 electrons mean an electronic configuration of 2,8,2
 • This means that the element is in Period 3 
 • It contains 2 outer electrons, which means that it is in Group 2

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A compound contains two atoms of oxygen and one atom of calcium. It also contains hydrogen in sufficient amounts so that the overall charge of the molecule is neutral.
 What is the molecular formula for the compound?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Calcium is in Group II so its valency is  +2 .
 • Oxygen and hydrogen bond together to form a  hydroxyl   ion , OH -
 • OH -  has an overall valency of  -1 , since oxygen is -2 and hydrogen is +1.
 • One Ca atom bonds with two OH -  ions to form the neutral compound Ca(OH) 2 .

options: A. Carbon dioxide is released when it reacts with a carbonate.
B. A salt is formed on reaction with an acid.
C. Ammonia is released on reaction with an ammonium salt.
D. Universal indicator paper turns blue when placed in an alkaline solution.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  
 Carbonates are  alkalis  and therefore do not react when added to a base.
 B  is incorrect as salt and water are formed in acid-base neutralisation reactions.
 C  is incorrect as ammonium salts decompose when warmed with alkalis, producing  ammonia gas , salt and water.
 D  is incorrect as all bases turn Universal Indicator paper  blue .

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  
 • In equation 1 substance X  accepts  a proton so is behaving as a base.
 • In equation 2 substance X  donates  a proton so it behaves as an acid.
 A ,  B  and  C  are incorrect as these options do not match with the behaviour of substance  X  in equations 1 and 2.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Copper(II) sulfate can be prepared by reacting solid copper(II) carbonate with hot sulfuric acid. The copper(II) carbonate is always added in excess.
 Why is the solid reactant added in excess?
options: A. To ensure all of the acid reacts.
B. To make the reaction go faster.
C. To ensure all of the solid reactant has reacted.
D. To increase the product yield.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  
 • Copper(II) carbonate reacts with sulfuric acid to produce copper(II) sulfate:
 • CuCO 3  + H 2 SO 4 → CuSO 4  + H 2 O + CO 2
 • Copper(II) sulfate is  soluble  and is separated from the mixture by  evaporation .
 • If there is any acid remaining in the solution it would become dangerously concentrated during this phase of the preparation.
 • For this reason the carbonate is added in excess to make sure that all of the acid has reacted.
 B  and  D  are incorrect as the rate of reaction and yield are not dependent on there being an excess of only one of the reactants.
 C  is incorrect as any unreacted copper(II) carbonate is removed by  filtration .

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Potassium and krypton are elements in Period 4. Potassium is at the beginning of the period and is more metallic than krypton which is at the end of the period.
 What makes potassium more metallic than krypton?
options: A. It has less electrons than krypton.
B. It has less protons than krypton.
C. It has less electron shells.
D. It has less outer shell electrons.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  
 • The change in metallic to non-metallic character as we move across the Periodic table from left to right is linked to the  electronic configuration  of the elements.
 • Non-metals have  more electrons  in their outer shells than metals.
 • Potassium is in  Group I  and has  1  electron in its outer shell whereas krypton is in  Group VIII  and has  8  electrons in its outer shell.
 A  and  B  are incorrect as although potassium has fewer electrons and protons than krypton, it is the  outer shell electrons  that determine its chemical properties.
 C  is incorrect as both elements are in the same period they have the same number of electron shells.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
An element has an electronic configuration of 2,8,6.
 Which group and period can the element be found in?
 |  
 | group
 | period
 |
 | A
 | 6
 | 3
 |
 | B
 | 6
 | 8
 |
 | C
 | 3
 | 6
 |
 | D
 | 8
 | 2
 |
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  
 • The electronic configuration shows the arrangement of electrons in their shells 
 • The last notation is the number of electrons in the outer shell 
 • The number of electrons in the outer shell correlates to the group number 
 • 2,8, 6  shows there are six electrons in the outer shell so the element is in Group 6 
 • The period number refers to the number of shells an atom has
 • The number of notations shows the number of shells
 • 2,8,6 has three notations so the element has three shells and is in Period 3 
 B ,  C  and  D  are incorrect as the group or period number is wrong

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of the following observations does not apply to Group I elements?
options: A. They are relatively soft metals.
B. They corrode quickly when exposed to air.
C. They react very quickly with water releasing hydrogen gas
D. They produce acidic solutions in reaction with water.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D
 • The Group I metals are also called the alkali metals and they produce  alkaline solutions  in reaction with water.
 • Lithium for example reacts to produce a lithium hydroxide solution which is alkaline, and hydrogen gas:
 • 2 Li (s) + 2 H 2 O (l) → 2 LiOH (aq) + H 2  (g)
 A ,  B  and  C  are incorrect as these are all characteristics of the  Group I  metals.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which reaction does  not  occur in the extraction of aluminium?
options: B. 2 Al 2 O 3  + 3 C → 4 Al + 3 CO 2
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Reaction A occurs at the cathode.
 • Reaction C occurs at the anode.
 • Reaction D occurs at the anode and is a result of hot oxygen bubbles reacting with the carbon electrodes.
 • Reaction B does not occur.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Calcium, copper, iron and magnesium are metals. They can be placed in order of reactivity.
 Which of the following statements about these metals is correct?
options: A. Iron reacts with steam but magnesium does not.
B. Copper reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to form copper (II) chloride.
C. Magnesium and calcium both react with hot water.
D. Iron (II) oxide cannot be reduced by heating strongly with carbon.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because  both magnesium and calcium are reactive enough to react with hot water.
 A  is incorrect as magnesium is more reactive than iron so would burn in steam producing magnesium oxide and H 2  gas.
 B  is incorrect as copper does not react with dilute hydrochloric acid
 D  is incorrect as iron (II) oxide is  reduced  with carbon in a blast furnace

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: The transition elements are used extensively as catalysts. Which statement explains why they are such good catalysts?
options: A. Their oxidation state does not change.
B. They have a large surface area.
C. They can have variable oxidation states.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  
 • The transition metals often have  various   oxidation  states, e.g. the common oxidation states of chromium are +2, +3 or +6.
 • This gives them the ability to easily  transfer electrons  to and from other species in a reaction.
 A  is incorrect as their oxidation state is variable and so can change.
 B  is incorrect as surface area is a physical property which can easily be increased by grinding metals into finer sized particles.
 D  is incorrect as they do form coloured compounds but this property is irrelevant to their catalytic ability.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The structure of an alloy is shown below. Alloys are mixtures of metals with other metals or non-metals.
  They are usually much stronger and harder than pure metals. Which statement explains these features?
options: A. The irregular sizes of the atoms distorts the regular arrangement in the metal structure, meaning more force is required to bend the metal
B. The irregular sizes of the atoms distorts the regular arrangement in the metal structure as the bonding is disrupted when the atoms are added
C. The regular sizes of the atoms distorts the irregular arrangement in the metal structure, meaning more force is required to bend the metal
D. A mixture of metals is tougher than a pure metal because a mixture has more intermolecular forces than a pure metal.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because  the distortment caused by the irregular sizes of the atoms makes it harder to force the layers of atoms in metals to slide over each other.
 B  is incorrect as bonding is not involved as an alloy is a mixture.
 C  is incorrect as the atoms in the mixture have irregular sizes while the pure metal structure consists of a regular pattern.
 D  is incorrect as in pure metals there are no intermolecular forces, only metallic bonding.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is C because:
 • When a metal reacts with an acid it produces a metal salt and hydrogen gas.
 • M(metal) + H 2 SO 4  → MSO 4  + H 2
 • The more reactive the metal the more hydrogen gas will be produced in the same amount of time.
 • The bar chart shows that metal T is the most reactive as this reaction produces the largest volume of gas, followed by Q.
 • The bar chart then shows the order of reactivity by the decreasing volume of hydrogen gas produced.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Aqueous sodium hydroxide is used in chemical analysis.
 Which statement about aqueous NaOH is correct?
options: A white precipitate is formed when added to a solution containing sulfate ions
B. A green precipitate is formed upon addition to a solution of iron(II) ions which does not dissolve in excess
C. A green precipitate is formed upon addition to a solution of iron(II) ions which dissolves in excess
D. An acidic gas is produced when added to ammonium chloride
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Iron(II) ions react with aqueous sodium hydroxide to produce a green-coloured precipitate which is iron(II) hydroxide:
 • Fe 2+  (aq) + 2OH –  (aq) → Fe(OH) 2  (s)
 • Iron(II) is insoluble in excess NaOH
 A  is incorrect as sodium sulfate is produced which is highly soluble, hence a precipitate is not formed
 C  is incorrect as the iron(II) hydroxide produced is insoluble in excess NaOH, hence it does not dissolve
 D  is incorrect as ammonia gas is produced which is basic, not acidic:  NH 4 Cl + NaOH → NaCl + NH 3  + H 2 O

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which pair of substances would make an NPK fertiliser?
options: A. ammonium phosphate and potassium chloride
B. calcium phosphate and potassium chloride
C. ammonium sulfate and potassium nitrate
D. potassium nitrate and calcium carbonate
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because: 
 • The elements present in an NPK fertiliser are nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium 
 • Ammonium phosphate, (NH 4 ) 3 PO 3  and potassium chloride, KCl provide these three elements 
 B  is incorrect as calcium phosphate and potassium chloride do not provide nitrogen
 C  is incorrect as ammonium sulfate and potassium nitrate do not provide phosphorus
 D  is incorrect as potassium nitrate and calcium carbonate do not provide phosphorus

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The production of sulfur trioxide during Stage 2 of the Contact process involves a reversible reaction. Which row describes the conditions of temperature and pressure and the percentage yield of sulfur trioxide?

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  
 • The conditions are  450   and  1 - 2 atm  pressure which provide a percentage yield of  98%.
 • A higher pressure is not used as it is too dangerous given that SO 3  is an  acidic  gas.
 • In economic terms it isn't worth the expense to use a higher pressure when a 98% yield is achievable at 1 - 2 atm.
 A, C  and  D  are incorrect as these options do not correctly describe the conditions used for the reaction.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Which is the correct reason for carrying out each step when treating water?
 |  
 |  Adding carbon
 |  Chlorination
 | Sedimentation
 |

 | kill microbes
 | remove salts
 | remove solids
 |

 | remove odours
 | kill microbes
 |
 | C
 | remove odours
 | kill microbes
 | remove solids
 |
 | D
 | remove odours
 | remove solids
 | remove salts

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Carbon is used to remove tastes and odours from water
 • Chlorine is used to kill microbes
 • Sedimentation is used to remove solids
 A  is incorrect as chlorine kills microbes and there should be a low level of dissolved salts in water 
 B  is incorrect as the purpose of all three steps are incorrect 
 D  is incorrect as sedimentation removes solids, not salts, and chlorine kills bacteria

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Carbon monoxide and steam react together exothermically to produce the alcohol methanol, as shown in the equation.
 CO(g) + 2H 2 (g) ⇌ CH 3 OH(g)
 Both reactants and the product are gaseous. Which conditions of pressure and temperature would provide the highest yield of CH 3 OH?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  
 • Increasing the temperature will shift the equilibrium in the direction of an  endothermic reaction .
 • The reaction is  exothermic , therefore an increase in temperature would favour the reverse reaction and decrease the yield of methanol.
 • From the balanced equation, there are  3  moles of reactants to  1  mole of product.
 • An increase in pressure would shift the equilibrium to the side with  less   volume , so it would favour the forward reaction and  increase  the yield of methanol.
 A ,  B  and  D  are incorrect as these conditions would not provide the highest yield of methanol.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The results of different chemical tests on a solution of compound  Y  are shown.
 | Test
 | Result
 |
 | Acidified barium nitrate added
 | White precipitate formed
 |
 | Aqueous sodium hydroxide added
 | White precipitate formed, soluble in excess
 |
 | Aqueous ammonia added
 | White precipitate formed, insoluble in excess
 |
 What is compound  Y ?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • Aluminium ions form a white precipitate with aqueous sodium hydroxide that is soluble in excess
 • Aluminium ions form a white precipitate with aqueous ammonia that is insoluble in excess
 • Sulfate ions form a white precipitate of barium sulfate when acidified barium nitrate is added
 B  is incorrect as chloride ions don't form a white precipitate with barium nitrate as barium chloride is soluble
 C  is incorrect as the white precipitate formed when aqueous ammonia is added to a solution containing zinc ions will dissolve in excess
 D  is incorrect as chloride ions don't form a white precipitate with barium nitrate as barium chloride is soluble. The white precipitate formed when aqueous ammonia is added to a solution containing zinc ions will dissolve in exces s

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which statement about the extraction of iron from its ore is  not  correct?
options: A. Iron can be extracted by reduction with carbon
B. Iron is easier to extract than zinc
C. Iron is easier to extract than copper
D. Iron is extracted from the ore, hematite
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because: 
 • Iron is higher up the reactivity series than copper 
 • The higher up the metal is, the harder it is to extract from its ore due to stronger bonds with its oxide
 A  is incorrect as iron is less reactive than carbon so can be extracted by reduction with carbon
 B  is incorrect as iron is easier to extract than zinc as it is lower in the reactivity series
 D  is incorrect as iron ore is called haematite

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Hydrocarbons separated by fractional distillation of petroleum can be cracked to make useful shorter chain products.
 Which substance is not a product of the cracking of propane,  M r   44?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 The process of  cracking  involves breaking large  hydrocarbon   molecules into smaller molecules.
 Cracking  alkanes can produce; a shorter chain  alkane  or  alkene  or 1 or more shorter  alkenes  and  hydrogen .
 The molecule C 4 H 8  has one more carbon and the original molecule of propane C 3 H 8 .
 B, C  and  D  are incorrect as all of these molecules could be a product of  cracking  of propane.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The apparatus below was used to test gas Y
  The bromine solution quickly went colourless.
 What is the correct structure of gas Y?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Gas  Y  is an alkene as it has a  carbon carbon   double bond.
 • The double bond in the alkene breaks and bromine is added to the molecule, this causes the  discolouration  of the bromine water.
 • This reaction shows  halogenation.
 A, B  and  D  are incorrect as none of these compounds have a  carbon carbon double bond.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The following reaction takes place in the presence of light.
 CH 4  + Cl 2  + light → CH 3 Cl + HCl
 What is the name for this reaction?
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Halogenation  is the replacement of one or more hydrogen atoms in an organic molecule by a  halogen  (fluorine, chlorine, bromine or iodine).
 • The  halogenation  of an alkane is an example of a  substitution reaction.
 A  is incorrect as the combination of  alkanes  with oxygen, generating heat is known as  combustion.
 B  is incorrect as  polymerisation  is the joining of simple single repeating units into a  polymer.
 C  is incorrect as  thermal decomposition  is the breakdown of a molecule using heat.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of these is an advantage of producing ethanol by fermentation of sugar compared to the catalytic addition of steam to ethene?
options: A. The process uses high temperatures.
B. The alcohol produced is purer.
D. The process uses renewable raw materials.
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Fermentation  is a metabolic process that produces  ethanol  from  glucose  and other sugars.
 • The sugars used in fermentation are from plants and so are a renewable resource.
 • Ethene  is extracted from petroleum (crude oil) and so is non-renewable.
 A, B  and  C  are incorrect as all of the processes are features of  ethanol  production from  ethene.

set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of the equations show the incomplete combustion of methane?
options: B. CH 4  + O 2   → C + 2 H 2 O
set-4/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Incomplete combustion  of  alkanes  in general produces carbon and/or carbon monoxide along with water
 • hydrocarbon + oxygen → carbon monoxide + carbon + water
 • Carbon dioxide is formed with a plentiful supply of oxygen, during complete combustion
 • Carbon monoxide is formed with a limited supply of oxygen
 • Carbon is formed with a  very  limited supply of oxygen
 • Exam questions will sometimes indicate if the product of incomplete combustion is carbon monoxide or carbon
 A  is incorrect as this is the balanced symbol equation for the  complete   combustion  of methane
 C  is incorrect as hydrogen is not a product of the combustion of alkanes
 D  is incorrect as this is not a balanced equation and has hydrogen gas as a product.

set-4/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:

set-4/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
Nitrogen dioxide is a brown gas. It can be made by heating certain metal nitrates.
 2Pb(NO 3 ) 2  → 2PbO + 4NO 2  + O 2
 At most temperatures, samples of nitrogen dioxide are equilibrium mixtures.
 2NO 2  (g)       N 2 O 4  (g)   dark brown            pale yellow
 i) At 25 °C, the mixture contains 20 % of nitrogen dioxide. At 100 °C this has risen to 90%. Is the forward reaction exothermic or endothermic? Give a reason for your choice.
 [2]
 ii) Explain why the colour of the equilibrium mixture becomes lighter when the pressure on the mixture is increased.
 [2]
set-4/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
i) The forward reaction is:
 • Exothermic;  [1 mark]
 • The forward reaction is favoured by low temperature / reverse reaction is favoured by high temperature;   [1 mark]
 ii) The colour of the equilibrium mixture becomes lighter when the pressure on the mixture is increased because:
 • The equilibrium shifts to the right / side of the product;   [1 mark]
 • Because this side has a smaller volume / fewer moles of gas produced;   [1 mark]
 [Total: 4 marks]
 • According to Le Chatalier's principle, when a change is made to a system, the system will shift the position of the equilibrium counteract the change
 • Be careful in part i)- the question states that more of the reactant is formed at high temperatures, the focus is not on the product
 • When temperature is increased, more reactant is formed so the system must have favoured the reverse reaction to decrease the temperature.
 • The reverse reaction is therefore endothermic and the forward reaction exothermic
 • You must give your ans

 [1]

 [2]
set-4/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
i) The term base  means :
 • Proton / H +  acceptor;  [1 mark]
 ii) You show that ammonia is the weaker base by:
 • (Measuring) pH / (using) universal indicator;  [1 mark]    Note: can be implied need not be explicit
 • Sodium hydroxide has high er  pH / ammonia has low er  pH;  [1 mark]   (This sentence would score 2 marks)
 OR
 • Appropriate colours with universal indicator / appropriate numerical values;  [1 mark]
 • Ammonia is closer to green, blue-green, turquoise or lighter blue / sodium hydroxide is darker blue / purple / violet;  [1 mark]
 OR
 • Measure electrical conductivity;  [1 mark]    Can be implied need not be explicit
 • Ammonia (aq) is the poor er  conductor / sodium hydroxide is the bett er  conductor;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 3 marks]
 • Sodium hydroxide is a strong base, a solution of sodium hydroxide would have a pH which is higher than the pH of a solution of a weaker base such as ammonia
 • Sodium hydroxide solution has a pH of around 13 (depending on concentration)
 •

set-4/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
Aluminium and iron are extracted from their ores by different methods.
 Aluminium is extracted from its purified oxide ore by electrolysis.
  What is the name of the ore of aluminium which consists mainly of aluminium oxide?
set-4/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
The name of the ore of aluminium which consists mainly of aluminium oxide is:
 • Bauxite;  [1 mark] 
 [Total: 1 mark] 
 • There are other ores of aluminium, however bauxite is used as it has the highest percentage of aluminium oxide
 • Roughly 4 tonnes of bauxite are required to make 1 tonne of aluminium

set-4/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
Use your copy of the Periodic Table to answer these questions.
 Choose an element from the Periodic Table to match each description. You may give either the name or the symbol.
 i) It is the most reactive metal.
 [1]
 ii) It is the only non-metal which is a liquid at r.t.p.
 [1]
 iii) This Group VII element is a solid at r.t.p.
 [1]
 iv) This element is in Group V and Period 4.
 [1]
 v) This unreactive gas is used to fill lamps.
 [1]
set-4/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
i) The element that is the most reactive metal is:
 • Cs / Fr;  [1 mark]
 ii) The element that is the only non-metal which is a liquid at r.t.p. is:
 • Br;  [1 mark]
 iii) The Group VII element that is a solid at r.t.p. is:
 • I or At;  [1 mark]
 iv) The element that is in Group V and Period 4 is:
 • As;  [1 mark]
 v) The element that is an unreactive gas used to fill lamps is:
 • He / Ne / Ar / Kr / Xe;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 5 marks]
 • Potassium is at the top of the reactivity series with sodium second, showing that the Group I metals are the most reactive of the metals
 • The reactivity of Group I metals increase as you down the group so the Group I metal at the bottom of the group will be the most reactive element
 • This is francium but caesium is also accepted, as there is such a small amount of francium found naturally (there is estimated to be about 30 g in the whole of the Earth's crust!)

set-4/paper-4-theory-extended.stem:
The structures of six organic compounds are shown.
  Give the name of  F .
set-4/paper-4-theory-extended.explanation:
The name of  F  is:
 • Butane;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 1 mark]
 • The main carbon chain / backbone contains 4 carbons
 • This means that the name will be based on "but-"
 • There are only single bonds and no other atoms apart from hydrogens
 • Therefore, the name will be "-ane" based
 • This leads to the overall name being butane

set-4/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.stem:
Ammonia is produced when aqueous sodium hydroxide is warmed with ammonium sulfate. Ammonia is less dense than air and very soluble in water. The apparatus below was used to prepare a sample of dry ammonia gas.
   Name substance  C .
set-4/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.explanation:
Substance  C  is:
 • Sodium hydroxide;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 1 mark]
 • Sodium hydroxide is a solution and ammonium sulfate is a solid (as it is an ionic compound which are usually solids)
 • The burette will hold the solution which is substance  C

set-4/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.stem:
A solid  U  was analysed.  U  was a soluble metal sulfate. The tests on  U , and some of the observations are in the following table.
 Complete the observations.
 | Tests
 | Observations
 |
 | Test 1 : Appearance of solid  U .
 | Pink crystals
 |
 | Test 2 : Solid U was heated gently and then strongly in a test-tube.
 | condensation droplets formed on the sides of the test-tube
 |
 | Solid  U  was added to distilled water in a test-tube and shaken until dissolved.
 |
 | Test 3 part (i) : The solution was divided into three equal portions in separate test-tubes and the following tests carried out. Several drops of aqueous sodium hydroxide were added to the first portion of the solution and the test-tube shaken.
 | pale brown precipitate
 |
 | Test 3 part(ii) : Then hydrogen peroxide solution was added to the mixture and the gas given off was tested.
 | effervescence glowing splint re-lit
 |
 | Test 4 : Dilute nitric acid was added to the second portion of the solution followed by barium nitrate solution.
 |  
 |
 | Test 5 : Dilute nitric acid was added to the third portion of the solution followed by silver nitrate solution.
 |  
 |
 i) State the expected observations for  Test 4 .
 [2]
 ii) State the expected observations for  Test 5 .
 [1]
set-4/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.explanation:
i) The observations for  Test 4  are:
 • White;  [1 mark]
 • Precipitate;  [1 mark]
 ii) The observations for  Test 5  are:
 • No reaction / no change / no precipitate;  [1 mark]
 Allow: colourless solution
 [Total: 3 marks]
 • Nitric acid followed by barium nitrate produces a white precipitate in the presence of sulfate ions, which is information given at the start of the question
 • There are no halide ions present, so there is no change and no precipitate formed when nitric acid and silver nitrate are added

set-4/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.stem:
The diagrams show the apparatus used to obtain crystals of calcium chloride from a mixture of solid calcium chloride and solid calcium carbonate. Calcium chloride is soluble in water and calcium carbonate is insoluble in water.
   Complete the boxes to name the apparatus.
set-4/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.explanation:
The names of the apparatus are:
 • Tripod;  [1 mark]
 • Stirring rod / stirrer;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 2 marks]
 • You should be familiar with both of these pieces of equipment and be able to name the other equipment used when making soluble and insoluble salts

set-4/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.stem:
Hydrochloric acid reacts with aqueous sodium thiosulfate to form a precipitate, which makes the solution turn cloudy. The formation of the precipitate can be used to show how fast the reaction proceeds, using the apparatus shown below.
  A student used this method to investigate the effect of changing the concentration of the sodium thiosulfate solution on the speed of the reaction. The student used different concentrations of sodium thiosulfate solution. All other variables were kept the same.
 Give  two  variables which were kept the same in the investigation.
set-4/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.explanation:
Two  variables which were kept the same in the investigation are:
 Any  two  from:
 • Volume;  [1 mark]
 • Concentration of acid;  [1 mark]   Allow amount
 • Volume of sodium thiosulfate / total volume of solution;  [1 mark]
 • Temperature;  [1 mark]
 • Printed sheet;  [1 mark]
 • Same size flask;  [1 mark]   Ignore reference to pressure / catalyst / surface area / light
 [Total: 2 marks]
 • This experiment is to investigate the effect of changing concentration of sodium thiosulfate solution on the speed of the reaction
 • The independent variable is the variable that you alter - in this case, the concentration of sodium thiosulfate solution
 • The dependent variable is the variable that you measure - in this case, the speed of the reaction
 • Everything else in the experiment should be kept the same so that the test is fair
 • It is not uncommon for students to name either the independent or dependent variable in this type of question, so be clear what they are and don't say you shoul

set-4/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.stem:
Look at the diagrams of common laboratory apparatus.
  Complete the empty boxes to identify the pieces of apparatus labelled.
set-4/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.explanation:
The pieces of equipment are:
 • A = mortar;  [1 mark]
 • B = stirrer / stirring rod;  [1 mark]   A thermometer is not accepted
 • C = tripod;  [1 mark]
 • D = Bunsen burner;  [1 mark]
 [Total: 4 marks]
 • The main issues with naming the equipment in this question are A and B
 • For A, the mortar (bowl) and pestle (stick) are commonly jumbled
 • For B, several students will put a thermometer even though a thermometer is used to measure temperature, not stir

set-4/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.stem:
A mixture of two solids,  E  and  F , was analysed. Solid  E  was the water-soluble salt aluminium chloride, AlCl 3 , and solid  F  was an insoluble salt. The tests on the mixture and some of the observations are in the following tables. Complete the observations in the tables.
 | tests
 | observations
 |
 | Distilled water was added to the mixture in a boiling tube. The contents of the boiling tube were shaken and filtered, keeping the filtrate and residue for the following tests.
 |  
 |
 | tests on the filtrate
 The filtrate was divided into five portions in five test-tubes.
 The first portion was used to describe the appearance of the filtrate
 | appearance ........................................ 
 |
set-4/paper-6-alternative-to-practical.explanation:
The appearance of the filtrate can be described as: 
 • Colourless;  [1 mark]    Ignore: clear, not: white
 [Total: 1 mark]
 • Aluminium chloride is water soluble so will dissolve in water but the insoluble solid  F  will remain as a solid
 • When the mixture is filtered, aluminium chloride is in solution so will pass through the filter, leaving the solid  F  on the filter paper
 • The solution that passes through filter paper is known as the filtrate
 • Aluminium does not form coloured compounds or solutions (transition metals give rise to coloured compounds and solutions but not other metals) so it will appear as a colourless solution

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Four substances are shown below. 
 In which of these substances are the particles close together and moving slowly past each other?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  
 • Particles which are  close together  but can  move  slowly past each other are in the  liquid  state.
 A  is incorrect as ice is a solid so the particles cannot move.
 B  and  C  are incorrect as air is a mixture of  gaseous  particles, and steam is water in the gaseous state, which move  faster  and are also  further  apart than particles in a liquid.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Measuring volumes of liquids is a fundamental aspect of experimental chemistry. The diagram shows three different pieces of apparatus used for this task.
  Which row is correct?
 |  
 | 1
 | 2
 | 3
 |
 | A
 | burette
 | measuring cylinder
 | pipette
 |
 | B
 | burette
 | pipette
 | measuring cylinder
 |
 | C
 | pipette
 | measuring cylinder
 | burette
 |
 | D
 | measuring cylinder
 | burette
 | pipette
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • 1 is a  burette  for carrying out  titrations .
 • 2 is a  graduated measuring cylinder  for measuring different volumes of liquids.
 • 3 is a pipette for measuring  fixed  and very  accurate  volumes of liquids.
 B ,  C  and  D  are incorrect as these names do not   match with the apparatus.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Pure H 2 O boils at 100  o C and freezes at 0  o C.
 What is the melting point and boiling point of water after the addition of potassium chloride?
 |  
 | Boiling point /  o C
 | Freezing point /  o C
 |
 | A
 | 103
 | -3
 |
 | B
 | 103
 | 3
 |
 | C
 | 97
 | -3
 |
 | D
 | 97
 | No change
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • Potassium chloride in water is an  impurity  which affects its physical properties.
 • Pure water boils at 100 ºC and freezes at 0 ºC.
 • In water, potassium chloride causes the boiling point to  increase  and the freezing point to  decrease .
 • This is why salt is used to prevent icing on roads as it lowers the freezing point, making it more difficult for ice to form at temperature close to 0 ºC.
 B  and  D  are incorrect as the freezing point of water  decreases  when potassium chloride is added to it.
 C  is incorrect as the boiling point of water  increases  when potassium chloride is added to it.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A student has performed an experiment which produced a precipitate. She correctly chooses to separate the precipitate using the process of filtration. She prepares the filter paper to be placed into the funnel by folding it as shown below.
  Which diagram correctly illustrates the filter paper at stage 3?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because: 
  • The first fold requires that the filter paper adopts a  semi-circular shape .
 • This is then folded again to form a cone that fits inside the funnel.
 B ,  C  and  D  are incorrect as these diagrams do not correctly illustrate the final step to obtain the required shape.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Most of the elements on the Periodic Table are metals. Metals can be distinguished from non-metals by differences in their physical properties.
 Which row correctly describes a metal?
 |  
 | Malleability
 | Heat & electrical conductivity
 |
 | A
 | 
 | 
 |
 | B
 | 
 | 
 |
 | C
 | 
 | 
 |
 | D
 | 
 | 
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Metals are  malleable  meaning they can be beaten into different shapes.
 • Metals also  conduct heat  and  electricity.
 A, B  and  D  are incorrect as metals have both of these properties due to the  close packing  of the metal ions and the  delocalised electrons.  Non-metals cannot conduct heat or electricity.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Element X contains 4 electrons in its outer shell and 125 neutrons in its nucleus. What is element X?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Elements are arranged on the Periodic table in  increasing atomic number  where each element has one proton more than the element preceding it.
 • The Group number gives the number of electrons in the  outer  shell of each element.
 • X is in Group  IV  so has four electrons in its outer shell.
 • X also has  125 neutrons , which corresponds to lead (Pb) only (as lead has a mass number of 207 and an atomic number of 82, so  207- 82 = 125 neutrons).
 A  is incorrect as beryllium has 2 electrons in its outer shell and carbon has 4 in its outer shell.
 B  is incorrect as although carbon has 4 electrons in its outer shell, it has a mass number of 12 and therefore only 6 neutrons in its nucleus (12 - 6 =6).
 C  is incorrect as tin has 69 neutrons, 119 - 50 = 69.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
CH 4 , H 2 O and HCl are covalent compounds.
 Which atoms in these compounds do not use all of their outer shell electrons in bonding?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 •   Oxygen  in water and  chlorine  in hydrogen chloride both have nonbonding electron pairs in their outer shells whereas methane does not as shown.
  A, B  and  D  are incorrect as in these options; there is either  carbon or hydrogen,  both of these atoms used all of their outer shell electrons in bonding.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which statement about graphite and diamond is not correct?
options: A. Graphite is a good lubricant due to the weak forces in between the layers.
B. Diamond is used as a drill tip because it is an extremely hard substance.
C. Graphite has a low melting point due to the weak forces in between the layers.
Diamond is an allotrope of carbon.
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because 
 • Graphite has a giant covalent structure and these compounds have  high melting points  due to the high number of covalent bonds holding atoms together within them.
 A  is incorrect as in graphite the carbon atoms are arranged in  layers  which can slide over each other easily as there are only  weak   forces  between the layers, making it useful as a lubricant.
 B  is incorrect as in diamond each carbon atom is covalently bonded to 4  others, forming a giant covalent structure. This makes it very hard as it requires a lot of energy to break so  many   strong   covalent  bonds and so it is useful as a tip for drills.
 D  is incorrect as diamond contains carbon atoms only and is in the  solid   state , hence it is an allotrope of carbon.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Dilute sulfuric acid and barium chloride solution react to produce barium sulfate and hydrochloric acid, as shown in the reaction below:
 H 2 SO 4  + BaCl 2  → BaSO 4  + 2 HCl
 Which row represents the correct state symbols for the reaction?
 |  
 | H 2 SO 4
 | BaCl 2
 | BaSO 4
 | HCl
 |
 | A
 | (aq)
 | (l)
 | (s)
 | (aq)
 |
 | B
 | (l)
 | (aq)
 | (aq)
 | (l)
 |
 | C
 | (aq)
 | (aq)
 | (s)
 | (aq)
 |
 | D
 | (l)
 | (aq)
 | (l)
 | (aq)
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Sulfuric acid is an  aqueous   solution  (all acids are in solution), so (aq) is the correct state symbol for H 2 SO 4
 • Barium chloride is a  soluble   salt  and dissolves easily in water, hence the symbol for BaCl 2  is (aq).
 • Barium sulfate is an  insoluble solid , so its state symbol is (s) and hydrochloric acid is  aqueous , so its state symbol is (aq).
 A ,  B  and  D  are incorrect as these options do not provide the correct state symbol for each species in the reaction.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Solid lead(II) bromide is heated until it is molten. The molten lead (II) bromide then undergoes electrolysis. 
 Which substances are formed at each electrode?
 |  
 | anode
 | cathode
 |
 | A
 | bromine
 | lead
 |
 | B
 | lead
 | bromine
 |
 | C
 | bromine
 | hydrogen
 |
 | D
 | hydrogen
 | lead
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • Molten metal bromides consist of positive metal ions and negative bromide ions 
 • The positive metal ion will be discharged at the cathode (negative electrode) where they will gain electrons to form the metal
 • The negative bromide ions will be discharged at the anode (positive electrode) where they will lose electrons to form bromine
 B ,  C  and  D  are incorrect as the products at the electrodes are incorrect

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which is true about chemical energy changes?
 |  
 |  Reaction type
 | Energy flows
 | Temperature of surroundings
 |
 | A
 | exothermic
 | to the surroundings
 | increases
 |
 | B
 | exothermic
 | from the surroundings
 | decreases
 |
 | C
 | endothermic
 | to the surroundings
 | decreases
 |
 | D
 | endothermic
 | from the surroundings
 | increases
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • In an exothermic reaction the energy transferred from the reacting chemicals heats up the surroundings and results in a rise in temperature
 B  is incorrect as the energy flow and temperature change are the wrong way around for an exothermic reaction
 C  is incorrect as the energy flow is the wrong way around for an endothermic reaction
 D  is incorrect as the temperature change is the wrong away around

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following processes represents a physical change?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  
 • A physical change involves a change in a  physical property .
 • Ethanol boils at 78  o C so at this temperature or higher it changes its physical state from a  liquid  to a  gas .
 A ,  B  and  D  are incorrect as these processes involve  chemical changes  where substances react together chemically, breaking and forming bonds.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A student was measuring the rate of reaction using the apparatus in the diagram.
  What reaction is the student studying?
options: A. CaO + H 2 SO 4  → CaSO 4  + H 2 O
C. Fe + H 2 SO 4  → FeSO 4  + H 2
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C
 • The diagram shows that the reactants are a  liquid  and a  solid .
 • The flask is  sealed  and a gas syringe is connected to the flask, hence one of the products must be a  gas .
 • C  is the only option that includes a solid (Fe) and liquid (H 2 SO 4 ) reactants, and a gaseous product (H 2 ).
 A, B  and  D  are incorrect as there are not any gaseous products formed in these reactions.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following statements is not correct?
options: Ammonia is released when a base reacts with an ammonium salt.
B. Neutralisation occurs when an acid and an alkali react together.
Carbon dioxide is released when an acid and a carbonate react together.
D. The higher the pH of a solution, the higher its acidity.
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  
 • Acids have  low  pH values and bases have  high  pH values.
 • The  lower  the  pH  value then the  higher  the  acidity  of the solution.
 A  is incorrect as ammonia gas is produced in this reaction:
 NH 4 Cl + NaOH →  NH 3  + NaCl + H 2 O
 B  is incorrect as acid-base reactions are  neutralisation  reactions.
 C  is incorrect as CO 2  is a product in this reaction:
 CaCO 3  + 2HCl → CaCl 2  +  CO 2   + H 2 O

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Different salts can be prepared by titrating an alkali with an aqueous acid.
 Three pieces of apparatus,  P ,  Q  and  R , used to measure volumes of liquid are shown below.
  What are the names of the three pieces of apparatus,  P ,  Q  and  R ?
 |  
 | P
 | Q
 | R
 |
 |  A
 | pipette
 | burette
 | measuring cylinder
 |
 |  B
 | burette
 | pipette
 | conical flask
 |
 |  C
 | pipette
 | volumetric flask
 | burette
 |
 |  D
 | burette
 | pipette
 | measuring cylinder
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D 
 • P  is a burette, it is used to add varying volumes which can be measured to a high degree of accuracy
 • Q  is a pipette, it is used to measure a specific quantity of liquid to a high degree of accuracy
 • R  is a measuring cylinder, it is used to measure volumes of liquids but the degree of accuracy is not as high as using a pipette or burette
 A  is incorrect as the names of  P  and  Q  are the wrong way round
 B  is incorrect as  R  is not a conical flask
 C  is incorrect as all of the names are incorrect

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Magnesium reacts with iron(III) oxide in the following reaction.
 magnesium + iron(III) oxide → magnesium oxide + iron
 Which statement about this reaction is correct?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  
 • Oxidation is defined as the gain of oxygen and reduction as the loss of oxygen
 • Magnesium is oxidised as it gains oxygen in the reaction to form magnesium oxide
 A  is not correct as magnesium oxide is a product formed by the oxidation of magnesium
 B  is not correct as iron is a product formed by the reduction of iron(III) oxide
 D  is not correct as iron(III) oxide is reduced as it loses oxygen to form iron

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which reaction would result in the production of a gas that would produce a squeaky pop with a lit splint?
options: B. Methane + oxygen during complete combustion
D. Carbon dioxide and water in the presence of light and chlorophyll
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • When magnesium reacts with hydrochloric acid, magnesium chloride and hydrogen gas are produced:
 • magnesium + hydrochloric acid → magnesium chloride + hydrogen
 • Hydrogen gas will produce a squeaky pop with a lit splint
 A  is incorrect as when iron(II) oxide and sulfuric acid react, iron(II) sulfate and water are produced in a neutralisation reaction. No gas is produced
 B  is incorrect as when methane and oxygen react during complete combustion, carbon dioxide and water are produced. No hydrogen is produced
 D  is incorrect as during photosynthesis, carbon dioxide and water react in the presence of light and chlorophyll to form oxygen and glucose. No hydrogen gas is produced

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A student is testing two substances,  P  and  Q , as shown.
  The results of the test are that the Universal indicator paper turns blue. What are substances  P  and  Q ?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  
 • In a reaction with an alkali and an  ammonium salt ,  ammonia  gas is produced.
 • P  and  Q  are sodium hydroxide and ammonium nitrate, which react together to produce sodium nitrate, water and  ammonia :
 • NaOH + NH 4 NO 3  → NaNO 3  + H 2 O +  NH 3
 • Ammonia gas is  alkaline  and turns damp Universal Indicator paper  blue .
 A  is incorrect as ammonium nitrate is a slightly acidic salt hence it will not react with another acid.
 C  is incorrect as sodium carbonate reacts with hydrochloric acid to produce sodium chloride, water and carbon dioxide gas:
 Na 2 CO 3  + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H 2 O + CO 2
 CO 2  gas is very slightly acidic and hence will not turn the indicator paper blue.
 D  is incorrect as both substances are alkaline and so do not react together.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
When an aqueous salt is crystallised, some water can be retained within the structure of the salt.
 What is the name given to the type of salt that forms?
 | A
 | anhydrous salt
 |
 | B
 | dehydrated salt
 |
 | C
 | hydrated salt
 |
 | D
 | soluble salt
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  
 • Salts that contain water within their structure are called hydrated salts
 A  is incorrect as anhydrous salts are those that contain no water in their structure
 B  is incorrect as dehydrated means to have lost water but these salts contain water
 D  is incorrect as soluble salts are able to dissolve in water

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which entry in the table matches the transition elements?
 |  
 | density
 | melting point
 | from coloured compounds
 |
 | A
 | high
 | low
 | no
 |
 | B
 | high
 | high
 | yes
 |
 | C
 | low
 | low
 | no
 |
 | D
 | low
 | high
 | yes
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  
 • The transition elements are  dense  metals with  high  melting points.
 • They form  coloured compounds .
 A  and  C  are incorrect as transition metals have  high melting points .
 C  and  D  are incorrect as they are dense metals which often have more than one oxidation state.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Element  X  is found in Group 7 of the Periodic Table. 
 Which properties are typical of element  X ?
 | 1
 | Poor conductor of electricity
 |
 | 2
 | Malleable
 |
 | 3
 | High melting points
 |
 | 4
 | Form acidic oxides
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  
 • Elements in Group 7 are non- metals
 • Non metals are poor conductors of electricity due to the lack of charged particles that can move freely 
 • Non- metals can also form acidic oxides 
 A ,  C  and  D  are incorrect as Group 7 elements typically have low melting points due to weak intermolecular forces between molecules and are not malleable

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The elements of the Periodic table can be broadly classified into two main characters which are metals and nonmetals. Which statements are correct?
 | 1
 | Magnesium is more metallic than silicon.
 |
 | 2
 | Boron is more metallic than lithium.
 |
 | 3
 | Carbon is less metallic than beryllium.
 |
 | 4
 | Sodium is less metallic than aluminium.
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  
 • Magnesium lies further to the  left  than silicon, hence it has a greater metallic character than silicon.
 • Beryllium is further  left  than carbon, hence it also has greater metallic character than carbon.
 B ,  C  and  D  are incorrect as as lithium and sodium are both more metallic than boron and aluminium as they lie further on the left of the Periodic table.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Element X is an unreactive non-metal element. Where could this element be found on the Periodic table?
options: At the far left hand side
B. At the far right hand side
C. At the top of Group VI
D. At the bottom of Group VII
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  
 • The  noble gases  are a group of unreactive non metal elements.
 • They are in Group VIII / 0 at the far right hand side of the table.
 A  is incorrect as this position corresponds to the Group I elements which are all  reactive metals .
 C  is incorrect as  carbon  sits at the top of Group VI and does react with other elements to form compounds.
 D  is incorrect as elements in Group VII are  reactive  and combine with other elements.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following observations does not apply to Group I elements?
options: A. They are relatively soft metals.
B. They corrode quickly when exposed to air.
C. They react very quickly with water releasing hydrogen gas
D. They produce acidic solutions in reaction with water.
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D
 • The Group I metals are also called the alkali metals and they produce  alkaline solutions  in reaction with water.
 • Lithium for example reacts to produce a lithium hydroxide solution which is alkaline, and hydrogen gas:
 • 2 Li (s) + 2 H 2 O (l) → 2 LiOH (aq) + H 2  (g)
 A ,  B  and  C  are incorrect as these are all characteristics of the  Group I  metals.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Which row in the table below shows how the metal will react?

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Magnesium will react with dilute hydrochloric acid to produce magnesium chloride and hydrogen gas.
 • Magnesium will react slowly with cold water
 • Magnesium burns in steam to produce magnesium oxide and hydrogen gas.
 A  is incorrect as copper will not react with dilute hydrochloric acid.
 B  is incorrect as calcium will react with dilute hydrochloric acid and slowly with cold water
 C  is incorrect as zinc will react with steam to produce zinc oxide and hydrogen gas.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Many metals can be extracted from their ores by heating the metal oxide with carbon.
 Which of these metals can’t be extracted using carbon?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because
 • Aluminium is more reactive than carbon.
 • The method used to extract a metal from its ore depends on the reactivity of the metal in the  reactivity series .
 • Metals lower than  carbon  in the reactivity series can be reduced by heating with carbon.
 • Metals above carbon in the reactivity series will either need to be reduced by another more reactive element or extracted via electrolysis.
 • Extraction by electrolysis is used to extract aluminium.
 A,   B  and  D  are incorrect as zinc, copper and iron are all below carbon in the reactivity series and can be extracted by reduction with carbon.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Properties of four elements are shown below.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Metals have high melting points as they have strong  metallic bonds.
 • Metals are able to conduct electricity when in a Option and  molten  state due to the presence of delocalised electrons.
 A  is incorrect as the melting point is below zero. This is too low to be a metal.
 B  is incorrect as metals conduct electricity when molten and in the solid state.
 D  is incorrect as the electrical conductivity of metals will be high both in a solid and liquid state.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Brass is an alloy of two metals
 Which is the correct statement?
options: A. The alloy will completely dissolve in dilute hydrochloric acid.
Brass is formed by a chemical reaction between two metals
C. Brass can be represented by a chemical formula
D. One of the metals in the alloy will dissolve in dilute hydrochloric acid
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc
 • Zinc is above hydrogen in the reactivity series so will react with dilute hydrochloric acid and will completely dissolve
 • Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series so will not react with dilute hydrochloric acid
 A  is incorrect as Copper in the alloy will not dissolve in dilute hydrochloric acid as copper is lower than hydrogen in the reactivity series
 B  is incorrect as Alloys are mixtures that do not involve a chemical reaction
 C  is incorrect as Alloys are mixtures, not compounds, so cannot be represented by a chemical formula

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Human activities increase the level of nitrogen oxides, sulfur dioxide and carbon dioxide in our atmosphere.
 Which row correctly shows the effect of each of these gases in our atmosphere?
 |  
 | Oxides of nitrogen
 | Sulfur dioxide
 | Carbon dioxide
 |
 | A
 | global warming
 | respiratory problems
 | photochemical smog
 |
 | B
 | acid rain
 | photochemical smog
 | respiratory problems
 |
 | C
 | photochemical smog
 | acid rain
 | global warming
 |
 | D
 | respiratory problems
 | global warming
 | acid rain
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Oxides of nitrogen cause photochemical smog and acid rain
 • Sulfur dioxide causes acid rain
 • Carbon dioxide causes global warming
 • Option  C  is the only option where the pollutant corresponds with these effects
 A ,  B  and  D  are incorrect as the effects do not correspond with the effects of each pollutant

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Reversible reactions occur when products formed in the forward reaction behave as reactants and proceed in the reverse direction to produce the original reactants again.
 Which of the following statements is correct for a reversible reaction?
 | 1
 | If the forward reaction is exothermic, then the reverse reaction must be endothermic
 |
 | 2
 | If the forward reaction is endothermic, then the reverse reaction must be exothermic
 |
 | 3
 | Both directions are exothermic
 |
 | 4
 | Both directions are endothermic
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  
 • The energetics of reversible reactions are such that if the forward direction is exothermic, then the reverse direction is the  opposite , hence endothermic.
 • This applies in both cases, so if the forward reaction is endothermic, then the reverse reaction must be exothermic.
 B  and  D  are incorrect as both directions will not have the same energy change.
 C  is incorrect as statements 1 and 2 are both true.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Mineral water contains dissolved salts such as magnesium chloride. Which one of the following statements about mineral water is correct?
options: A. Mineral water boils at slightly above 100 °C.
B. Mineral water is pure water.
C. Mineral water boils at exactly 100 °C.
D. Another name for mineral water is fizzy water.
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because dissolved salts raise the boiling point of water
 B  is incorrect because pure water means water without anything dissolved in it
 C  is incorrect because the boiling point of water is affected by the dissolved minerals, so the boiling point cannot be 100  o C
 D  is incorrect because fizzy water refers to water with dissolved carbon dioxide; many types of mineral waters are fizzy but not all fizzy water is mineral water. Soda water is fizzy water, but is not mineral water.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The diagram below shows the apparatus used to separate petroleum (crude oil) into four fractions.
  Which fraction contains the smallest hydrocarbon molecules?
 | fraction
 | boiling point range / °C
 |
 | A
 | up to 70
 |
 | B
 | 71 to 120
 |
 | C
 | 121 to 170
 |
 | D
 | over 171
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because
 • The boiling point of the hydrocarbon depends on the  molecular   mass . The  larger  the molecular  mass  the  higher  the  boiling   point .
 • Larger molecules have more  intermolecular   forces  which hold the molecules together, so more energy is needed to overcome these forces for a state change.
 • Smaller molecules have less intermolecular forces between the molecules so need less energy to overcome these forces.
 B, C  and  D   are incorrect because they all have boiling points above A and therefore bigger molecules.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the equations show the incomplete combustion of methane?
options: B. CH 4  + O 2   → C + 2 H 2 O
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Incomplete combustion  of  alkanes  in general produces carbon and/or carbon monoxide along with water
 • hydrocarbon + oxygen → carbon monoxide + carbon + water
 • Carbon dioxide is formed with a plentiful supply of oxygen, during complete combustion
 • Carbon monoxide is formed with a limited supply of oxygen
 • Carbon is formed with a  very  limited supply of oxygen
 • Exam questions will sometimes indicate if the product of incomplete combustion is carbon monoxide or carbon
 A  is incorrect as this is the balanced symbol equation for the  complete   combustion  of methane
 C  is incorrect as hydrogen is not a product of the combustion of alkanes
 D  is incorrect as this is not a balanced equation and has hydrogen gas as a product.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
The blast furnace is used to extract iron from haematite.
  The haematite contains silica as an impurity
 What is used to react with the impurity and remove it?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Impure iron contains impurities of carbon, phosphorus, silicon and sulfur.
 • Oxygen is blown in to  oxidise  the impurities to their oxides in a basic oxygen converter.
 • Calcium oxide is used to remove the silicon and phosphorus oxides to produce slag:
 • SiO 2  + CaO → CaSiO 3
 • The slag floats to the surface of the molten iron and is removed.
 A  is incorrect as carbon reacts with oxygen in a combustion reaction, heating the blast furnace forming carbon dioxide: C + O 2  → CO 2
 C  is incorrect as carbon dioxide is produced in the reaction of carbon with oxygen.
 D  is incorrect as oxygen reacts with carbon in a combustion reaction, heating the blast furnace forming carbon dioxide:  C + O 2  → CO 2

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of the following statements about ethanol is  not  correct?
options: A. It is formed by a reaction between steam and ethane.
B. It can be used as a fuel.
C. It can be used as a solvent.
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because  ethanol is formed by the  catalytic hydration  of  ethene,  not ethane.
 B  is incorrect as the complete combustion of  ethanol  in excess oxygen produces carbon dioxide and water and heat, so it can be used as a fuel:
 C 2 H 5 OH +3O 2  → 2CO 2  + +3H 2 O
 C  is incorrect as  ethanol  is an important solvent in many industrial processes.
 D  is incorrect as the  functional group  of alcohol is -OH

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Car exhausts release oxides of nitrogen (NO and NO 2 ) and carbon monoxide, CO
 • Power stations release carbon dioxide, CO 2 , sulfur dioxide, SO 2 , and carbon monoxide, CO
 • Therefore all of these XO could be nitrogen oxide or carbon monoxide 
 • YO 2  could be carbon dioxide, nitrogen dioxide, or sulfur dioxide

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A student carried out a cracking reaction on hydrocarbon,  P , and obtained two products;  Q  and  R .
  The student then made the following notes:

 | Q  is unsaturated.
 |
 | 2
 | R  will decolourise bromine water.
 |
 | 3
 | A molecule of  P  has 7 carbon atoms.
 |
 Which of the statements are correct?
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • R  will decolourise bromine water.
 • Compound  R  is an  alkene  with a  carbon carbon double bond .
 • This will react with the  bromine water  in a  halogenation  reaction.
 • P  has  7  carbon atoms:
 • The process of  cracking  involves breaking large  hydrocarbon   molecules into smaller molecules.
 • The total number of carbon atoms in the two smaller molecules is  7 . Carbon atoms are not lost in the reaction.
 A, B  and  D  are incorrect as Q is not unsaturated, this has no  carbon carbon double bonds . Q will be an alkane, butane.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which statement about aqueous sodium hydroxide is correct?
options: A. When added to a solution containing nitrate ions and aluminium foil then warmed, the gas given off will bleach moist red litmus paper
B. When added to a solution containing iodide ions, a yellow precipitate is formed
C. When added to a solution of iron(II) ions, a green precipitate is formed which dissolves in excess sodium hydroxide to form a green solution
D. When added to a solution containing aluminium ions, a white precipitate forms which dissolves in excess sodium hydroxide to form a colourless solution
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • When sodium hydroxide reacts with aluminium ions, it forms a white precipitate
 • The precipitate will dissolve in excess sodium hydroxide to form a colourless solution
 A  is incorrect as when added to a solution containing nitrate ions and aluminium foil and then warmed, ammonia will be given off which will turn moist red litmus paper blue
 B  is incorrect as it is silver nitrate that will form a yellow precipitate when added to a solution containing iodide ions
 C  is incorrect as the green precipitate does not dissolve in excess sodium hydroxide

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which of these statements about carboxylic acids is  not  correct?
options: Aqueous ethanoic acid has a pH less than 7.
B. Methyl orange turns yellow in aqueous ethanoic acid.
C. They produce carbon dioxide when reacted with a metal carbonate.
D. They contain the functional group -COOH.
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Aqueous ethanoic acid is a  weak acid.
 • A weak acid only partially dissociates in an aqueous solution. Remember pH is a measure of the concentration of hydrogen ions in solution.
 • Methyl orange  is an  indicator  that changes from orange to yellow in the pH range of 3.1 - 4.4.
 • The pH of ethanoic acid is higher than the range detected by methyl orange.
 A, C  and  D  are incorrect as all of the statements correctly describe carboxylic acids.

set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
A macromolecule is a very large molecule.
 Macromolecules can be made by joining smaller molecules together. This is called  polymerisation.

 |
 | D
 | ethene
 | poly(ethane)
 |
set-5/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • The carbon carbon double bonds open up and form long chain molecules called  polymers.
 • The resulting polymer produced from ethene monomers is called poly(ethene) or polythene.
 A  and  C  are incorrect as these are alkanes and have no double bonds.
 D  is incorrect as when ethene undergoes polymerisation it becomes poly(eth e ne), not poly(eth a ne).

set-5/paper-3-theory-core.explanation:

set-5/paper-3-theory-core.stem:
Choose a gas from the following list to answer the questions below. Each gas may be used once, more than once or not at all.

 Which gas
 i) Is a noble gas?
 [1]
 ii) Is an acidic oxide?
 [1]
 iii) Can be polymerised?
 [1]
 iv) Is the active component of air?
 [1]
 v) Is used in the treatment of water?
 [1]
set-5/paper-3-theory-core.explanation:
i) The noble gas is:
 • Argon;  [1 mark] 
 ii) The acidic oxide is:
 • Carbon dioxide;  [1 mark]
 iii) The gas that can be polymerised is
 • Ethene:  [1 mark] 
 iv) The active component of air is:
 • Oxygen;  [1 mark] 
 v) The gas used in the treatment of water is:
 • Chlorine;  [1 mark] 
 [Total: 5 marks]
 • The noble gases are found in group 8 / 0 of the Periodic table 
 • Carbon dioxide is an acidic oxide, do not get confused with carbon monoxide which is a neutral oxide 
 • Alkenes can be polymerised to form polymers, the alkene behaves as a monomer and undergoes addition polymerisation
 • The composition of air is:
 • 78% nitrogen
 • 21% oxygen
 • 0.9% argon
 • 0.04% carbon dioxide 
 • Oxygen is the most reactive of these gases
 • Chlorine is used in small amounts in the treatment of water to kill pathogens 
 • It is a toxic substance, but only small amounts are used so it will not pose a risk to health

set-5/paper-3-theory-core.stem:

set-5/paper-3-theory-core.stem:
A student investigates the reaction of small pieces of zinc with dilute sulfuric acid at 20 °C.   The zinc is in excess.   Sulfuric acid is a compound.
 Define the term compound.
set-5/paper-3-theory-core.explanation:
A compound is:

set-5/paper-3-theory-core.stem:
Iron is extracted from its ore, hematite, in a blast furnace.
 Substances added to the furnace are:
 • Iron ore, hematite, containing impurities such as silica, SiO 2
 • Air
 • Coke, C
 • Limestone, CaCO 3
 Substances formed in the blast furnace are:
 • Molten iron
 • Molten slag
 • Waste gases such as carbon dioxide
 State the  two  functions of the coke used in the blast furnace.
set-5/paper-3-theory-core.explanation:
The  two  functions of the coke used in the blast furnace are:
 • A reducing agent;  [1 mark] 
 • A source of energy / heat;  [1 mark]

 • Coke is burnt in the blast furnace to produce heat from the following reaction
 • C + O 2  → CO 2
 • This reaction is followed by
 • CO 2  (g)  +  C (s)  →  2CO (g)
 • CO is used as the reducing agent to then form the iron from iron oxide

set-5/paper-3-theory-core.stem: Give three differences in physical properties between the Group I metal, potassium, and the transition element, iron.

a) Three differences in physical properties between the Group I metal, potassium, and the transition element, iron are:

 • Iron has higher melting / boiling point;  [1 mark]

 NOTE: has to be comparison, e.g. iron is hard [0 marks] but iron is harder [1 mark]

 • Most metals share some properties, such as conduct electricity or are shiny, but the Group I metals and transition elements have their own properties which can be used to distinguish them
 • This question relies on you knowing the properties for both Group I metals and transition elements and identifying the differences
 • NOTE : As the question asks for you to give differences, it is very important that your

set-5/paper-3-theory-core.stem:
Islay is an island off the west coast of Scotland. The main industry on the island is making ethanol from barley.
 Barley contains the complex carbohydrate, starch. Enzymes catalyse the hydrolysis of starch to a solution of glucose.
 Yeast cells are added to the aqueous glucose. Fermentation produces a solution containing up to 10% of ethanol.

  ii) Explain why is it necessary to add yeast and suggest why the amount of yeast in the mixture increases.

 • Glucose → carbon dioxide + ethanol;  [1 mark]

 The amount of yeast in the mixture increases because:

 iii) A higher temperature not used in this process because:
 • Heat / high temperature would kill yeast (cells)   OR   Heat / high temperature denatures enzymes;  [1 mark]   Enzymes being killed or yeast being denatured are not accepted answers
 • Which would reduce the rate of reaction / slow the reaction / stop the reaction   OR   Which means that there is no catalyst / (yeast or enzyme) no longer catalyses   OR   No more product is formed;  [1 mark]

 • This question is showing the clear overlap between Biology and Chemistry in the process of fermentation, applying the

set-5/paper-3-theory-core.stem:
Molten potassium bromide can be electrolysed. Predict the products of this electrolysis at:
 the anode the cathode
set-5/paper-3-theory-core.explanation:
The products of electrolysis are:
 • At the anode: bromine / Br 2 ;  [1 mark] 
 • At the cathode: potassium / K;  [1 mark] 
 [Total: 2 marks] 
 • Electrolysed  molten  potassium bromide will split up into potassium and bromine gas
 • Potassium ions and bromide ions are formed when potassium bromide is melted (becomes a liquid)
 • The positive potassium ions are attracted to the negative electrode (cathode) and potassium atoms are formed
 • The negative bromide ions are attracted to the positive electrode (cathode) and bromine gas is formed

set-5/paper-3-theory-core.stem:

 Name the salt formed when calcium carbonate reacts with hydrochloric acid.

 • To name a salt, the first part of the name is taken from the metal in the metal / metal oxide / metal hydroxide / metal carbonate 
 • The second part of the name comes from the acid:
 • Nitric = nitrate
 • Sulfuric = sulfate
 • Hydrochloric = chloride

set-5/paper-3-theory-core.stem:

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • Potassium chloride in water is an  impurity  which affects its physical properties.
 • Pure water boils at 100 ºC and freezes at 0 ºC.
 • In water, potassium chloride causes the boiling point to  increase  and the freezing point to  decrease .
 • This is why salt is used to prevent icing on roads as it lowers the freezing point, making it more difficult for ice to form at temperature close to 0 ºC.
