set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Element X contains 4 electrons in its outer shell and 125 neutrons in its nucleus. What is element X?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • Elements are arranged on the Periodic table in  increasing atomic number  where each element has one proton more than the element preceding it.
 • The Group number gives the number of electrons in the  outer  shell of each element.
 • X is in Group  IV  so has four electrons in its outer shell.
 • X also has  125 neutrons , which corresponds to lead (Pb) only (as lead has a mass number of 207 and an atomic number of 82, so  207- 82 = 125 neutrons).
 A  is incorrect as beryllium has 2 electrons in its outer shell and carbon has 4 in its outer shell.
 B  is incorrect as although carbon has 4 electrons in its outer shell, it has a mass number of 12 and therefore only 6 neutrons in its nucleus (12 - 6 =6).
 C  is incorrect as tin has 69 neutrons, 119 - 50 = 69.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which statement about graphite and diamond is not correct?
options: A. Graphite is a good lubricant due to the weak forces in between the layers.
B. Diamond is used as a drill tip because it is an extremely hard substance.
C. Graphite has a low melting point due to the weak forces in between the layers.
Diamond is an allotrope of carbon.
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because 
 • Graphite has a giant covalent structure and these compounds have  high melting points  due to the high number of covalent bonds holding atoms together within them.
 A  is incorrect as in graphite the carbon atoms are arranged in  layers  which can slide over each other easily as there are only  weak   forces  between the layers, making it useful as a lubricant.
 B  is incorrect as in diamond each carbon atom is covalently bonded to 4  others, forming a giant covalent structure. This makes it very hard as it requires a lot of energy to break so  many   strong   covalent  bonds and so it is useful as a tip for drills.
 D  is incorrect as diamond contains carbon atoms only and is in the  solid   state , hence it is an allotrope of carbon.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
CH 4 , H 2 O and HCl are covalent compounds.
 Which atoms in these compounds do not use all of their outer shell electrons in bonding?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 •   Oxygen  in water and  chlorine  in hydrogen chloride both have nonbonding electron pairs in their outer shells whereas methane does not as shown.
  A, B  and  D  are incorrect as in these options; there is either  carbon or hydrogen,  both of these atoms used all of their outer shell electrons in bonding.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

 • Barium chloride is a  soluble   salt  and dissolves easily in water, hence the symbol for BaCl 2  is (aq).
 • Barium sulfate is an  insoluble solid , so its state symbol is (s) and hydrochloric acid is  aqueous , so its state symbol is (aq).

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Magnesium nitride and water react to produce a precipitate of magnesium hydroxide and ammonia gas.
 Mg 3 N 2  + 6 H 2 O → 3 Mg(OH) 2  + 2 NH 3

The correct answer is  B :

 | Working out
 |

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The diagram shows the electrolysis of aqueous copper(II) sulfate.
  Which statement is correct?
options: A. Copper metal is deposited at the positive electrode.
B. In the external circuit the electrons move from negative to positive.
C. In the solution the electrons move from positive to negative.
D. Oxygen gas is produced at the positive electrode.
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • The ions present in the electrolysis of aqueous copper(II) sulfate are: H +  and OH -  (from the aqueous solution), Cu 2+   and SO 4 2-
 • The H +  and Cu 2+  ions are attracted to the cathode and the OH -  and SO 4 2-  ions are attracted to the anode.
 • At the cathode (negative electrode) the Cu 2+  ions are less reactive than the hydrogen  ions and are reduced to copper metal:
 • Cu 2+  + 2 e -  → Cu
 • At the anode (positive electrode) the OH -  ions are less reactive than SO 4 2-  ions are oxidised to produce oxygen and water:
 • 4 OH -  → O 2  + H 2 O + 4 e -
 A  is incorrect as copper ions are positive so copper metal is produced at the negative electrode (the cathode), not the positive electrode.
 B  is incorrect as electrons in the external circuit begin at the negative terminal of the  battery and flow around the circuit and back to the positive terminal.
 C  is incorrect as the electrons do not flow in the electrolyte, it is the ions tha

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • During the electrolysis of concentrated aqueous sodium chloride,  positively   charged   hydrogen   ions  are attracted to the  negative   cathode  where they are reduced to form hydrogen gas.
 • At the  positive   anode , the Cl -  ions are oxidized to form chlorine gas.
 • The ions that remain in solution are Na +  ions and the OH -  ions.
 • These produce an  alkaline  solution so at the  cathode  the colour is  blue .
 • At the  anode  the solution is surprisingly colourless. This is because chlorine gas is a powerful bleaching agent and removes the colour from litmus.
 A, B  and  C  are incorrect as these colours do not match with the correct results.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of the following processes represents a physical change?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  
 • A physical change involves a change in a  physical property .
 • Ethanol boils at 78  o C so at this temperature or higher it changes its physical state from a  liquid  to a  gas .
 A ,  B  and  D  are incorrect as these processes involve  chemical changes  where substances react together chemically, breaking and forming bonds.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
The graph shows the results of two separate reaction rate investigations using excess calcium carbonate and sulfuric acid.
  Which statement explains the difference between the results?
options: A. The temperature was higher in experiment 2.
B. Experiment 2 was allowed more time to react.
C. Same volume of a more concentrated acid was used in experiment 2.
D. More calcium carbonate was used in experiment 2.
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  
 • The curve for the experiment 2 indicates that it produced a  higher volume  of gas in a shorter period of time.
 • This indicates that the rate of reaction was  faster  in experiment 2 than in experiment 1.
 • As the reaction rate was quicker and the volume of product was greater, then there must have been  more   acid  used since the calcium carbonate was in excess.
 A  is incorrect as a higher temperature would produce a  steeper  curve.
 B  is incorrect as both reactions were allowed  sufficient  time to react.
 D  is incorrect as the calcium carbonate was in  excess  in  both  experiments.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Endothermic reactions can be used in emergency sports injury treatment packs.
 What is true about these packs?
options: Absorb energy from the surroundings and transfer it to the injury
C. Usually contain ammonium nitrate and water in separate compartments
D. Cause the temperature of the surroundings to increase
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Most sports injury cold packs contain ammonium nitrate and water which react endothermically when mixed
 A  is incorrect as these are endothermic reactions and absorb energy from the injury to reduce swelling
 B  is incorrect as the reactions are not reversible so the packs can only be used once
 D  is incorrect as the temperature of the surroundings will decrease when the pack is activated

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A student wishes to electroplate an object with copper.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  D  because:
 • In electroplating, the anode is always the metal that is being used to coat the other metal.
 • Coating occurs as the  positive metal ions  are attracted to the object to be coated, which is the  negatively charged cathode .
 • The object to be coated is thus the  cathode  which attracts the  Cu 2+  ions.
 • The electrolyte used is an aqueous solution of a soluble salt of the pure metal at the anode.
 • In this case a solution of copper sulphate is suitable.
 A  and  B  are incorrect as the object to be coated is the cathode, not the anode.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A student is testing two substances,  P  and  Q , as shown.
  The results of the test are that the Universal indicator paper turns blue. What are substances  P  and  Q ?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  
 • In a reaction with an alkali and an  ammonium salt ,  ammonia  gas is produced.
 • P  and  Q  are sodium hydroxide and ammonium nitrate, which react together to produce sodium nitrate, water and  ammonia :
 • NaOH + NH 4 NO 3  → NaNO 3  + H 2 O +  NH 3
 • Ammonia gas is  alkaline  and turns damp Universal Indicator paper  blue .
 A  is incorrect as ammonium nitrate is a slightly acidic salt hence it will not react with another acid.
 C  is incorrect as sodium carbonate reacts with hydrochloric acid to produce sodium chloride, water and carbon dioxide gas:
 Na 2 CO 3  + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H 2 O + CO 2
 CO 2  gas is very slightly acidic and hence will not turn the indicator paper blue.
 D  is incorrect as both substances are alkaline and so do not react together.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A substance reacts with dilute H 2 SO 4  to form a salt which is separated by filtration.
 What is the substance?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  
 • Barium sulfate is  insoluble  and hence can be removed by filtration.
 • This salt will be the solid product that remains in the filter paper afterwards.
 A  is incorrect as all sodium salts are  soluble
 C  and  D  are incorrect as copper sulfate is a  soluble  salt.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: In which reaction is the reactant being reduced?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  
 • Reduction is the  gain of electrons .
 • Mg 2+  gains 2 electrons and its oxidation number changes from  +2  to  0 , hence it has been reduced.
 A  is incorrect as Mg loses electrons hence is  oxidised .
 C  is incorrect as oxidation occurs since the oxidation number of Cr  increases  from +2 to +3.
 D  is incorrect as C has gained oxygen so it has been  oxidised .

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which statement about the Alkali metals is correct?
options: A. Potassium is more dense than lithium.
B. Lithium has a higher density than sodium.
C. Potassium is less reactive than sodium.
D. The melting point of sodium is higher than lithium.
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  
 • The atomic number of the elements increases and their properties change as you move down Group I.
 • Melting and boiling points and hardness  decrease  while their density  increases .
 • They become  more   reactive  due to increasing distance between the outermost  electrons and the nucleus, making it easier for the metals to lose their outer shell electron.
 • Potassium is below lithium in Group I so its density is  higher  than that of lithium.
 B  is incorrect as lithium is  less dense  than sodium as it is higher up in the group.
 C  is incorrect as potassium is below sodium in Group I and is thus  more   reactive .
 D  is incorrect as sodium has a  lower  melting point than lithium since it is lower down the group.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which equation does  not  show the correct reaction of an acid?
options: B. CaCO 3  + HNO 3  → CaNO 3  + CO 2  + H 2 O
C. 2KOH + H 2 SO 4  → K 2 SO 4  + 2H 2 O
D. Zn + H 2 SO 4  → ZnSO 4  + H 2
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  
 • When a metal carbonate and acid react, a salt, carbon dioxide and water are formed
 • In option B, the formula for calcium nitrate is wrong and the equation is not balanced
 • The correct equation is:
 CaCO 3  + 2HNO 3  → Ca(NO 3 ) 2  + CO 2  + H 2 O
 • The correct formula for calcium nitrate is Ca(NO 3 ) 2
 • Ca 2+  and NO 3 –  are the ions, so two nitrate ions are required to form a neutral ionic compound

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Element X is an unreactive non-metal element. Where could this element be found on the Periodic table?
options: At the far left hand side
B. At the far right hand side
C. At the top of Group VI
D. At the bottom of Group VII
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  
 • The  noble gases  are a group of unreactive non metal elements.
 • They are in Group VIII / 0 at the far right hand side of the table.
 A  is incorrect as this position corresponds to the Group I elements which are all  reactive metals .
 C  is incorrect as  carbon  sits at the top of Group VI and does react with other elements to form compounds.
 D  is incorrect as elements in Group VII are  reactive  and combine with other elements.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Element Q is a halogen which reacts with aqueous potassium bromide, as shown in the reaction below:
 Q 2  + 2 KBr → 2 KQ + Br 2

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:

 • Element Q has displaced bromine from the compound KBr, so it must therefore be more reactive than bromine as reactivity  decreases  moving down Group VII.
 • The atomic mass also  increases  moving down the group as subatomic particles are added on.
 • Element Q is thus  more   reactive  than bromine and has a  lower  relative atomic mass.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

 |

 |

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  
 • Magnesium lies further to the  left  than silicon, hence it has a greater metallic character than silicon.
 • Beryllium is further  left  than carbon, hence it also has greater metallic character than carbon.
 B ,  C  and  D  are incorrect as as lithium and sodium are both more metallic than boron and aluminium as they lie further on the left of the Periodic table.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Why are alloys harder than the pure metals from which they are made?
options: A. There are stronger bonds between the atoms
B. The atoms are all the same size
C. The layers of atoms are distorted
D. The properties of each element have combined
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Alloys are mixtures of metals
 • The different metals have different sized atoms which means the atoms are no longer arranged in rows
 • The layers of atoms become distorted so that if pressure is applied, the layers cannot slide over each other making the alloy harder and stronger
 A  is incorrect as they are harder because of the distorted layers of atoms
 B  is incorrect as the atoms of each element in the alloy are of different sizes
 D  is incorrect as the properties of each element have not been combined

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: A student analysed a solution and found it to contain ions of silver and barium. What could the identity of the anion be?
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • The question states that the solution contains both Ba 2+  and Ag +  ions, so the anion with which they are combined must be water soluble
 • Only nitrates of both barium and silver are soluble in water 
 B  and  D  are incorrect as  BaSO 4  is insoluble in water as are the carbonates of silver and barium
 C  is incorrect as AgCl is insoluble in water

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • The melting point of aluminium oxide is 2030ºC.
 • By dissolving it in molten cryolite, the melting point is reduced to 900 - 1000ºC.
 • The lower temperature is more cost effective and safer to operate.
 • The aluminium ions are positively charged and are deposited at the negatively charged electrode, the cathode.
 A  and  B  are incorrect as the cryolite is molten and not aqueous.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
A student prepared four iron nails as explained below in an experiment to investigate rusting. She allowed the nails to rest in individual test tubes in a laboratory for one week.
 Which nail will show the greatest amount of rust?
options: A. Dipped in water and allowed to dry.
B. Dipped in paint and allowed to dry.
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because:
 • Rusting is the corrosion of iron in the presence of  oxygen  and  water  to produce  iron   oxide :
 • 4 Fe (s)  + 3 O 2 (g) +  x H 2 O(l) → 2 Fe 2 O 3● H 2 O(s)
 • Both oxygen and water  must  be present and in contact with the surface of the nail for it to rust.
 • Nail A will rust quite quickly as there is nothing protecting its surface.
 B  and  C  are incorrect as these nails will not rust as the paint and grease coatings act as  protective barriers , so oxygen and water cannot get into contact with the surface of the nail.
 D  is incorrect as zinc is a more  reactive metal  and more likely to lose electrons than iron. It readily donates its electrons to any iron ions that might have formed, stopping them from corroding.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Mineral water contains dissolved salts such as magnesium chloride. Which one of the following statements about mineral water is correct?
options: A. Mineral water boils at slightly above 100 °C.
B. Mineral water is pure water.
C. Mineral water boils at exactly 100 °C.
D. Another name for mineral water is fizzy water.
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  A  because dissolved salts raise the boiling point of water
 B  is incorrect because pure water means water without anything dissolved in it
 C  is incorrect because the boiling point of water is affected by the dissolved minerals, so the boiling point cannot be 100  o C
 D  is incorrect because fizzy water refers to water with dissolved carbon dioxide; many types of mineral waters are fizzy but not all fizzy water is mineral water. Soda water is fizzy water, but is not mineral water.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Petrol engines produce pollutants as a by-product of internal combustion. Catalytic converters are fitted to cars to reduce the level of pollution they produce in their exhaust gases.
 Which statement about this process is  not  correct?
options: A. Nitrogen and oxygen react to produce nitrogen dioxide.
B. Carbon monoxide undergoes oxidation in the catalytic converter.
Carbon monoxide is formed when petrol undergoes complete combustion.
D. Nitrogen monoxide undergoes reduction in the catalytic converter.
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • Carbon monoxide is a product of the  incomplete combustion  of a hydrocarbon.
 • Incomplete combustion occurs when there is a lack of oxygen, which can occur in the confined spaces of a car engine.
 • An example of incomplete combustion is methane:
 • 2 CH 4 (g) + 3 O 2 (g) → 2 CO(g) + 4 H 2 O(g)
 A  is incorrect as nitrogen and oxygen from the air react in the hot and cramped conditions in engines.
 B  and  D  are incorrect as these statements accurately describe the processes that occur inside a catalytic converter.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

 • The forward reaction is  endothermic  as energy is needed to decompose the molecule and remove the water of crystallisation.
 • In reversible reactions, if the forward reaction is endothermic then the reverse reaction is  exothermic  (and vice versa).
 • Anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride turns  blue  to  pink  when water is added.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem: Which of these statements about carboxylic acids is  not  correct?
options: Aqueous ethanoic acid has a pH less than 7.
B. Methyl orange turns yellow in aqueous ethanoic acid.
C. They produce carbon dioxide when reacted with a metal carbonate.
D. They contain the functional group -COOH.
set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  B  because:
 • Aqueous ethanoic acid is a  weak acid.
 • A weak acid only partially dissociates in an aqueous solution. Remember pH is a measure of the concentration of hydrogen ions in solution.
 • Methyl orange  is an  indicator  that changes from orange to yellow in the pH range of 3.1 - 4.4.
 • The pH of ethanoic acid is higher than the range detected by methyl orange.
 A, C  and  D  are incorrect as all of the statements correctly describe carboxylic acids.

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:

set-6/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is  C  because:
 • There is a carboxylic acid group (-COOH) and an amine group(-NH 2 ) at either end.
 • The link between these two functional groups is the amide link and each one is formed as a water molecule is lost, hence the name condensation polymerisation.
 • There is a water molecule removed in the process shown in the question, therefore it is produced by condensation polymerisation.

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:
Water boils at 100 °C to form steam.
 Which statement about the particles of steam is correct?
options: A. The arrangement of the molecules is regular.
B. The molecules move quickly in random directions.
C. The forces of attraction between the molecules are strong.
D. The molecules are close together.
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is B
 • Steam is water in  gaseous state
 • The particles of a gas move randomly at high speeds
 A  &  D  are incorrect because gases have a random arrangement of particles that are far apart between each other
 C  is incorrect because the forces of attraction are the weakest between the three states of matter

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which statement about diffusion is correct?
options: A. It is a chemical change.
B. The net movement of particles is from a region of lower concentration to a region of higher concentration.
C. The particles spread in order with a fixed pattern.
D. The net movement of particles is from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is D
 • Diffusion involves the random movement of particles, resulting in an  overall (net)  movement down the concentration gradient
 B  &  C  are incorrect because they are opposites to the diffusion definition
 A  is incorrect because diffusion is a physical change since it does not involve a change in the bonds of the substance that diffuses

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which diagram shows a mixture of compounds?
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is C
 • A  compound  consists of two or more different elements  chemically bonded  together
 • Mixtures are combinations in which substances are not chemically combined
 • One compound is represented by two black circles and one white circle
 • The other compound is represented by one black circle and one white circle
 • The two different types of compounds are  not chemically bonded  to each other
 A  &  B  are incorrect because both of them just contain one substance, so they are not mixtures
 D  is incorrect because it shows a  mixture of elements  because the particles are single, unbonded atoms of different types

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem: Which statement about carbon is correct?
options: B. It has 2 outer shell electrons.
D. It has an electron configuration of 2,8,2.
set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.stem:

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is C
 • Statement 1 is incorrect  because propane is an  alkane , while propanol is an  alcohol , so they belong to different homologous series
 • Propane (C 3 H 8 ) is an alkane, meaning it contains only single C–C bonds with enough C-H bonds to complete four bonds per carbon
 • Propanol (C 3 H 7 OH) is an alcohol because it contains the –OH functional group
 • Substances in the same homologous series must have the same functional group, so propane and propanol are not in the same homologous series
 • Statement 2 is correct  because propanol has the  prefix prop- , which means it contains three carbon atoms in the main carbon chain
  • Statement 3 is incorrect  because propane is a  saturated  hydrocarbon, not unsaturated
 • A hydrocarbon is unsaturated only if it contains a carbon–carbon double bond (C=C)
 • Propane contains only single bonds because it is an alkane, so it is a saturated hydrocarbon

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:

 • Hydrocarbons with  high boiling points  (long-chain molecules)  condense low down  in the column
 • Hydrocarbons with  low boiling points  (short-chain molecules)  rise higher  before condensing
 • As chain length increases, hydrocarbons have  stronger intermolecular forces
 • Stronger intermolecular forces mean  higher boiling points ,  higher viscosity , and  lower volatility
 • This explains why fractions with longer carbon chains are more viscous liquids 
 • Therefore, the viscosity of the fractions increases as chain length increases, so C is correct

set-7/paper-1-multiple-choice-core.explanation:
The correct answer is A
 • Silver nitrate reacts with sodium chloride to form silver chloride, which is insoluble and appears as a white precipitate

set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.stem:
Ethanol can be manufactured by fermentation or by the catalytic addition of steam to ethene
 Three statements comparing these two processes are shown.
 • The hydration of ethene uses non-renewable raw materials, whereas fermentation uses renewable raw materials. 
 • Hydration is carried out as a batch process, making it less efficient than fermentation. 
 • Hydration requires high temperatures and pressures, whereas fermentation requires a low and controlled temperature.
 Which statements are correct?
set-8/paper-2-multiple-choice-extended.explanation:
The correct answer is B

 • Statement 2 is incorrect
 • Hydration is a  continuous process , which is very fast and efficient
 • Fermentation is a  batch process  which is slow and inefficient because the reaction vessel must be emptied and cleaned after every batch

 • Fermentation requires a low, controlled temperature (typically 25–35 °C) because higher temperatures would denature the yeast enzymes acting as the catalyst
